In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

These are among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a), which are built on pausing (al-waqf), unlike the verses of the Qur'an, which, as we have said, are built on continuity (al-wasl) from the beginning of the Qur'an to its end, indeed on joining its end to its beginning. Therefore you should recite the Qur'an with continuity, as long as your breath helps you, and pause only when your breath runs out; then you pause and make silent the letter on which you paused.

The scholars of qira'at (the readings) have said: "There is nothing in the Qur'an that requires a pause (waqf wajib), because it is built on continuity; so do not pause unless your breath is constrained." Accordingly, they set out places for pausing, and they are marked in the mushaf (صلى، قلى، ج), but the original principle is continuity.

We have said that the clearest example of continuity in the Qur'an is the word al-nas at the end of Surat al-Nas, which is the last of the Qur'an. It did not come with a sukun, but with a kasra (al-nasi), because Allah the Exalted has ordained your journey (halluka) in al-Nas, so that you journey to "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" at the beginning of al-Fatiha. Thus the connection between the end of the Qur'an and its beginning is not severed. For this reason we have called the reciter of the Qur'an "the one who journeys" (al-hal al-murtahil).

Here comes ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim (1)﴾ [al-Sajda], after the five keys of the unseen (mafatih al-ghayb) that preceded at the end of Surat Luqman, as if it were appended to them. It is a secret which Allah the Exalted has kept to His own knowledge, and in our explanation of it we circle around it. Therefore, everyone who explains the disjointed letters at the beginning of the surahs must say after them: "And Allah knows best what He intends," because all our explanations are efforts that circle around the intended meaning. For this reason we do not say this phrase in all the verses of the Qur'an, but only in these verses and these letters in particular.

And how will it be with us when Allah the Exalted gathers us, if Allah wills, in a seat of truth before a Sovereign, Omnipotent? How will it be with us when we hear this Qur'an directly from Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Without doubt we will hear many words other than those we have heard, and many meanings other than those we have reached in our efforts. Then we will know the intentions of Allah the Exalted in these letters, and we will know how much our minds fell short of understanding them, and how foolish we were in our understanding of the intentions of our Lord.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 32, verse 2:

The Almighty's words ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ [As-Sajdah] are usually followed by a matter that concerns the Mighty Book.

Here He, glorified is He, says:

﴿The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, is from the Lord of the worlds.﴾

The root (nazala) occurs in the Qur'an in the forms nazala, nazzala, and anzala. Anzala (to send down) indicates causation, meaning that Allah, exalted is He, caused the Qur'an to be transferred from the Preserved Tablet until it begins its task in the lowest heaven, and this sending down is from Allah, exalted is He.

As for nazzala (to reveal gradually), the tanzil (gradual revelation) is the task of the angels. Therefore, regarding the sending down, He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ [Al-Qadr], that is, from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven. Then the angels bring it down piece by piece according to events. Concerning this He, exalted is He, says: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 193].

He, glorified is He, also says: ﴿And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended...﴾ [Al-Isra' 105]. It was preserved with Us in the Preserved Tablet, ﴿which none touches except the purified﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 79], and then the Trustworthy Spirit, Jibril, brought it down.

Since ﴿nazala bihi﴾ [it was brought down with him] [Ash-Shu'ara' 193] means that the Qur'an descended with him, his saying ﴿nazala bihi al-ruhu al-amin﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 193] is exactly equivalent to ﴿And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended﴾ [Al-Isra' 105]. Thus the descent is attributed at one time to the Qur'an and at another time to the Trustworthy Spirit.

The root nazala and what derives from it, such as inzal and tanzil, all indicate that it came from a higher place down to a lower place, as if you are receiving from one who is above you and higher. Since you are receiving from a place higher than you, beware lest thought lead you astray toward another direction.

Therefore, He, exalted is He, addressing His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the matter of obligation, says: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you...﴾ [Al-An'am 151]. We understand that ta'alaw (come) means ta'al (come). That is: approach. But it carries with this meaning the sense of height: approach, being brought close to the Exalted, rise from your earthly circumstances to the exaltation of your Lord in the Highest Assembly.

Ta'al means: do not take from yourself, nor from one equal to you, but rise and take from the Highest. Rise above the level of the earth and its people's minds and thoughts, and take from the One who legislated for you, because He must have matters and attributes that are safer and more secure for you, since His knowledge is broader, so He does not legislate for you today what He will annul tomorrow.

Moreover, His legislation for you encompasses all aspects of your life and its affairs, and these attributes exist only in the True One, blessed and exalted is He. He, glorified is He, is more merciful to you than a mother to her child, so He legislates for you only what benefits you. Furthermore, He, glorified is He, has no purpose or personal interest behind this legislation, as we see in human legislation for humans.

We have seen the capitalists, when they enacted a law that came to serve them, and so that they would be the first to benefit from it, it swiftly collapsed, because the condition of a true legislator is that he does not himself benefit from what he legislates. Accordingly, there is no true legislator except Allah.

Therefore we see that even those who do not believe in Allah, from among the disbelievers or polytheists, after events bite them and their laws fail to solve their problems, they resort to solutions drawn from the laws of Islam.

When we were asked in San Francisco about His saying: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it﴾ [At-Tawbah 33], and in another place: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will complete His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [As-Saff 8].

They said to us: this means that Islam has been dominant over the religions for fourteen centuries, so why do we now see most of the people of the earth being non-Muslims?

I replied to them: By Allah, if you understood the secrets of the language and contemplated this verse, you would find the answer in it. One says ﴿even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [As-Saff 8], and the other says ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it﴾ [At-Tawbah 33].

So disbelief and polytheism exist alongside the existence of Islam, and the meaning of prevalence here is not that these people be wiped out or that they be decisively eliminated. Rather, it prevails over them in such a way that they are compelled to it and resort to its rulings, despite not believing in it. This is a more eloquent form of prevalence: that you adopt what is in the Qur'an while you do not believe in it, because you find no solution to your problems except in it.

The clearest example of this is that they attacked the law of Allah concerning divorce and concerning polygamy, and accused Islam of savagery, etc. Then the demands of life and its problems compel them to legislate divorce and to practice it in plain view of the Vatican. What happened then? We say to them: Have you become Muslims and believed? No, we only resorted to it, because in it is the solution to these problems that surrounded us.

This, then, is the testimony of the enemy to the religion of Allah, and this is the greatest manifestation of Islam over these religions, because if they had embraced Islam, they would have said of them: they adopted this law because they became Muslims. Instead, here they are, adopting it while they are disbelievers and polytheists.

The meaning of ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [As-Sajdah 2] is: there is no uncertainty in it. We have said that propositions concern the relation of one thing to another, and that the relation is either affirmed with certainty or not affirmed with certainty. If we say: the earth is spherical, this is a proposition we now affirm with certainty, and we can demonstrate its validity by sensible evidence; this is an established proposition, affirmed with certainty, and there is evidence for it from the universe.

If the proposition is not affirmed with certainty, it falls into three states: either there is doubt (shakk), or conjecture (zann), or wishful thinking (wahm). Doubt is when the two pans, affirmation and negation, are equal. Conjecture is when the affirmative side prevails, so you do not affirm it with certainty but prefer it. If the other side overcomes and you make it the preponderant one, this is delusion (tawahhum).

Here He, glorified is He, said ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [As-Sajdah 2]: no uncertainty in it. He negated doubt, which is the equality of negation and affirmation. Since He negated equality, this means He intended to affirm the higher state, that is, that it is a truth to which doubt cannot ascend.

The phrase ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [As-Sajdah 2] is a parenthetical clause between ﴿the Book﴾ [As-Sajdah 2] and ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [As-Sajdah 2]. And since it is ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾, it must be a truth in which there is no doubt.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 32, verse 3:

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, so that they may be guided.﴾

It is strange that the Arabs should meet the Word of God with this accusation, when they are a people of eloquence, rhetoric and clear expression, and had reached a great standing in this field, to the point that they made markets (ma'arid) and fairs (aswaq) for speech, just as we now hold exhibitions for our products, and only the goods that are a source of pride are displayed at these exhibitions. Before Islam, 'Ukaz and Dhu al-Majaz were an arena (midmar) for speech and for expressive performance among men of letters and poets.

So it is strange of them that they cannot distinguish the speech of God from the speech of men, especially since He challenged them and challenged their eloquence and rhetoric to bring forth a single verse like it. It is well known that a challenge is issued to the strong, not to the weak, so the Qur'an's challenge to the Arabs counts in their favour; it is an acknowledgment of their standing and the standing of their language. It is, therefore, a testimony in their favour, and it is enough for them that God, exalted is He, included them with Himself in the field of challenge.

When they were unable to produce its like, they turned to accusing it and accusing the Messenger of God. Sometimes they say: "A poet." Sometimes: "A sorcerer." At other times they say: "A madman." And at other times they say: "Rather, some non-Arab is teaching him..." etc. All of this is bankruptcy of argument. They wished to deny the Messenger of God (ﷺ), but as for the Qur'an itself, it was not hidden from them that it is the speech of God, and that men do not produce speech like this. The proof is that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, when he heard it, said: "By God, its upper part is fruitful, and its lower part is abundant, and it is lofty and nothing is loftier than it" (1).

Therefore, when they found no flaw in the Qur'an, they acknowledged that it is from God, but their objection was that it should be sent down upon this particular man: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?"﴾ [az-Zukhruf] So they were expecting that the Qur'an would be sent down upon one of their great men or one of the kings, but that it should be sent down upon Muhammad, this orphan and poor man, did not please them. The Qur'an has answered them: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others by degrees...﴾ [az-Zukhruf]

That is: if We have apportioned among them the affairs of this world and what they excel in of its goods, shall We leave to them the affairs of the Hereafter to apportion as they wish and as their whims dictate? Prophethood is a mercy from God that He bestows upon whom He wills of His servants: ﴿God knows best where to place His message...﴾ [al-An'am].

This means that they came to the conclusion that the Qur'an is inimitable, and that it is from God beyond any doubt. And the one among them who read it and became certain that it is true said: ﴿O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Anfal]

This is a statement that no sensible person would make, and it indicates their stupidity and foolishness. It would have been more fitting for them to say: "O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then guide us to it."

The Qur'an has answered all their fabrications against the Messenger of God, refuted them all and showed their falsehood. When they said of the Messenger of God that he was mad, God answered them: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character.﴾ [al-Qalam]

A madman can never be of great moral character, because he is governed by instinct; he does not choose between alternatives and conduct as an animal does, and noble character does not arise from this.

As for the sound human being, he chooses between many alternatives. If a person wrongs him, he may respond with the same kind of wrong; he may reflect on requital, and that his retaliation might increase the harm, so he inclines toward forbearance. One restrains his anger, and another removes every trace of anger and seeks his reward for that from God, in obedience to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you not love that God should forgive you?﴾ [an-Nur] as though God were encouraging us to do good.

Therefore, when al-Hasan al-Basri was asked: "How can God ask us to do good to one who has wronged us?" he said: "These are the stages in the domain of virtues, and God has permitted you to repay an evil with its like: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ [ash-Shura] but He leaves the door open before the generosity of the believing soul: ﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God...﴾ [ash-Shura]"

Then, if we weigh this matter by the measures of reason, all creatures are the dependents of God, and they are equal in His sight. So what if one of your dependents wrongs another? There is no doubt that you would stand on the side of the wronged one, take him into your embrace, care for him and show him compassion. Likewise, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, stands on the side of His servant when he is wronged. One of them said: "Shall I not do good to one whom God has placed on my side?"

From here they say: "You do not gain much from the good people; rather, all your gain comes from the wicked when they wrong you and you do good to them." Therefore they say: "So-and-so is a good man, but whoever walks with him never benefits from him in any good at all. Why? They say: Because he serves everyone, and has made his cheek a doormat (mudas) for those who are with him, so that no one can gain (yastaftih) any good from him."

It is related from our master the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he smiled in a gathering with his Companions, and they said: "What makes you laugh, O Messenger of God?" He said: "I saw my Lord, and two adversaries were made to sit before Him. One of them said: 'O Lord, this one has wronged me, so take my right from him.' He said: 'How shall I take your right from him?' He said: 'Give me of his good deeds in proportion to what he did to me.' He said: 'He has no good deeds.' He said: 'Then take of my sins and cast them upon him.' He said: 'Would it satisfy you that you have no sin?' He said: 'Then, O Lord, how shall I settle my right with him?' He said: 'Look to your right.' The man looked to his right and found palaces, gardens and paradises, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to a human heart. He said: 'For whom are these, O Lord?' He said: 'For whoever pays their price.' He said: 'And what is their price, O Lord?' He said: 'That you take your brother by the hand and bring him into Paradise.' Then I marvelled at a Lord who reconciles between His servants" (4).

This concerns their saying about the Messenger of God that he is mad. As for their saying that he is a sorcerer, the refutation of it is easy: if Muhammad were a sorcerer who bewitched those who believed in him, then why did he not bewitch you too? Your being safe from sorcery is proof that he (ﷺ) is not a sorcerer, rather this is a lie and a fabrication against the Messenger of God.

As for their saying that he is a poet, this is strange of them, for they are a people of speech and eloquence, and they are the people of God most able to distinguish poetry from prose, and the best at distinguishing styles and modes of expression. God, exalted is He, Himself undertook the refutation of them, saying: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him.﴾ [Ya-Sin]

And in Surat al-Haqqah, He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Nor is it the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.﴾ [al-Haqqah]

When all these stratagems failed and all these fabrications were disproved, they said: "Rather, he has a devil who teaches him." They used to say this of the eloquent poet who had no rival in eloquence and excellence of expression, to the point that they assigned to these jinn a special place of their own, and called it "the Valley of 'Abqar," which is the dwelling of those jinn who inspire men and teach them.

Poetry is measured, rhymed speech, and it has known metres (buhur). Is the Qur'an of this sort? No; rather, it is a fabrication against the Messenger of God, like their fabrication against him here:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?...﴾ [as-Sajdah]

God's saying ﴿Or do they say...﴾ [as-Sajdah] — "am" (or) indicates that it has a counterpart, meaning: Do they say such-and-such? Or do they say, "He has invented it"? So what is this counterpart? The counterpart is: ﴿The revelation of the Book, in which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [as-Sajdah]. The meaning is: Do they believe that this Book is from the Lord of the worlds, and that there is no doubt in it? Or do they say that Muhammad invented it? So "am" here has come to negate what precedes it in speech.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord...﴾ [as-Sajdah] — we know that "bal" (rather) comes for correction, but here it is not for correction; rather, it is to nullify their saying "He has invented it," as if you said: "Zayd is not with me, rather 'Amr," so it indicates a turning away from what precedes it and the affirmation of the ruling for what follows. They say "He has invented it," and God says: ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord...﴾ [as-Sajdah]. So their speech and their accusation are false, and the Qur'an is the truth from God.

We have said that ﴿al-Haqq﴾ [the truth] (as-Sajdah) is the established thing that is not subject to change. Therefore realities are fixed and never change. How? Suppose an incident occurred, from which emerged a plaintiff, a defendant and witnesses, and they all gathered before the judge. It may happen that one of them changes his statements, or the witnesses give false testimony.

But the judge's experience and training uncover the realities and expose their lies when he sets their statements against one another, questions them and debates with them until he reaches the truth. This is because reality is one thing; even if they describe a reality, they would agree on it. The judge's skill is what exposes the contradictory falsehood, nullifies it, and establishes and prevails with the truth that cannot be contradictory.

Like the judge before whom two adversaries gathered, one of whom claims against the other that he took money from him and did not return it. The defendant said: "Rather, I returned it to him in such-and-such a place." The plaintiff denied it. The judge said to the defendant: "Go to this place; perhaps this money fell from you there." The man went and was slow for some time. The judge said to the plaintiff: "Your companion has been slow." He said: "He was slow because the place is far." Thus he fell into the very truth he had been denying.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿That you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you﴾ [as-Sajdah]. It is well known that our master the Messenger of God came as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but here the warner is singled out, because he came to correct corrupt beliefs, and the correction of what is corrupt must precede what is promised as good news. The mention of good tidings is not made here because they did not listen to the warning and did not benefit from it.

But His saying: ﴿to whom no warner has come before you﴾ [as-Sajdah] verbally seems to clash with His saying: ﴿And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir] and His saying: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra']. There is no contradiction among these verses, because the meaning is: no near warner had come to them, and there is no objection to the existence of a distant warner, as He says: ﴿O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you, after a gap in the messengers...﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

Otherwise, from where did they know that God, exalted is He, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "God." Say: "Praise be to God."﴾ [Luqman]. This is a trace of the earlier messengers, for among them there were people who followed the method of the true religion, whom God called the hanifs, who did not prostrate to an idol and did not deviate from the sound natural disposition (fitrah).

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that they may be guided﴾ [as-Sajdah]. "La'alla" (so that/perhaps) expresses hope, and hope from God is as though it were a realized fact, because God, exalted is He, loves for all His servants that they should believe in Him, so that they may receive the goodly gifts of His bounty in the Hereafter, just as they received His gifts in this world; and they are all His creation and His handiwork. We have already mentioned the sacred hadith: "...Leave Me with what I have created; whoever turns to Me, I love him; and if he does not repent..."

(1) A group of Quraysh gathered with al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and he said to them: "O assembly of Quraysh, this season has come, and the delegations of the Arabs will come to you in it, and they have heard about the affair of your companion (meaning Muhammad). So agree upon one opinion regarding him, and do not differ, lest some of you call others liars." Some said: "He is a soothsayer." Another said: "He is mad." Another said: "He is a poet." Another said: "He is a sorcerer." He rejected all their statements, then said: "By God, his speech has sweetness, its root is fruitful, its branch is bountiful, and whatever you say of it will be known to be false. The closest thing you can say about him is that he is a sorcerer who brought a speech that is sorcery, by which he separates a man from his father, a man from his brother, a man from his wife, and a man from his kin." So they dispersed from him on that account. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/284)]

(2) The scholars differed in identifying the great man intended. From Mecca: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira or 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah. From al-Ta'if: 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud or 'Umayr ibn 'Abd Yalil. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/127): "The apparent meaning is that they meant a great man from whichever of the two towns." The two towns here are Mecca and al-Ta'if.

(3) This verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he swore that he would never benefit Mistah ibn Uthathah with anything after he had spoken about 'A'ishah. When God revealed the innocence of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, God moved al-Siddiq to show kindness to his relative and kinsman Mistah, who was the son of al-Siddiq's maternal aunt, and who was a poor man with no wealth except what Abu Bakr spent on him. The hadd punishment had been applied to him for the slander he had committed against 'A'ishah. Then God revealed His saying: ﴿Do you not love that God should forgive you?﴾ [an-Nur]. At that, al-Siddiq said: "Yes, by God, we love that You forgive us, our Lord," and he went back to Mistah and resumed the support he had been giving him. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/276]

(4) Narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (4/576), who said: "Its isnad is sahih, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi said: "'Abbad is weak, and his shaykh is not known." Likewise Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya al-Sijistani recorded it in "al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur" (pp. 49, 50), both from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 32, verse 4:

Then the Exalted and Glorified (al-Haqq subhanahu) moves us to a matter of the fundamental principles of the cosmos:

﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He istawa (rose over) the Throne. For you there is not, besides Him, any protector or intercessor. Then will you not remember?﴾ (32:4)

The Exalted and Glorified Lord informs us that He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them for the service of man, who is the first honoured one in this cosmos, and all the kinds of creation are in his service: animals, plants and inanimate things. So he is a master (sayyid) in this cosmos. But did this master take his mastery by his own essence and by his own action? No, he took it only by the grace of Allah upon him, so it was incumbent upon him first to be grateful to the One who gave him this mastery above anyone else.

This master's life and his passage through this world is a crossing ('ubur). His lifespan in it, whether long or short, ends in death, whereas the inanimate things that serve him have a lifespan longer than his, and they are serving him. So it was obligatory upon him to reflect on this matter: how can the servant's lifespan be longer and more enduring than the lifespan of the master who is served?

Therefore: there must be for me another lifespan longer than this, a lifespan that befits Allah's honouring of me and befits my mastery in this cosmos. It is the Hereafter, where these creatures that served me in the world will perish while I remain. I do not live with the means (al-asbab), but with the Causer (al-musabbib), glory be to Him. So I do not need the means that served me in the world; rather I find everything I desire before me without fatigue and without striving, and these are elevations that are attained only by one who obeys the Giver who elevates.

Accordingly, the Exalted and Glorified Lord draws our attention and says: True, you, O man, are the master of this cosmos and all My creatures are at your service, but the creation of them is greater than your creation:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ (40:57)

Why? Because people have fixed lifespans; however long they last, they must end at a term. Moreover, these lifespans are not secure for them, but are subject to changes: the wealthy may become poor, the healthy may fall ill, the strong may weaken. As for the sun, the moon, the stars and the whole cosmos, they are not exposed to these changes. We have never seen the sun, the moon or the stars afflicted by a sickness and then ending as man ends. Furthermore, you are not like them in comprehensive admonition, for the most you can do is serve yourself or serve the environment around you, whereas these creatures serve the whole cosmos.

So if even the disbelievers acknowledge that Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, then it is the first proof of the existence of the Truth, blessed and exalted.

The matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth is among the things whose knowledge Allah has reserved for Himself, and no one may say: how did He create? Nor even how man was created, because matters of creation were not witnessed by anyone so as to inform us of them. Therefore the Exalted says:

﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take misleaders as helpers.﴾ (18:51)

So He named them misleaders (mudillun), and the one who misleads is the one who inclines you toward false paths and turns you away from the truth. We have indeed seen these misleaders and heard their fabrications concerning the matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth.

Therefore, the creation of the heavens and the earth is a matter that can only be taken from the One who created. That is why our Lord, blessed and exalted, related to us the story of the creation of Adam, and related to us the story of the creation of the heavens and the earth. But creation is an event and an act, and an act requires a time in which the event is processed and carried out. The difficulty here lies in His saying ﴿in six days﴾ (32:4), so does the event, with respect to the Exalted, require time?

An act by a human requires a process that takes time, where we distribute the parts of the act over the parts of time. But with regard to Him, the Exalted, He acts without processing affairs; rather He says to a thing "Be," and it is. As for His saying ﴿in six days﴾ (32:4), we have clarified it with an example, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness.

We have said: when you make yogurt, for instance, you bring milk, then you add to it yogurt culture prepared earlier, then you leave it at a certain temperature for seven or eight hours, after which you find the milk has turned into yogurt. Do you say: the making of the yogurt took me seven or eight hours? No; it only took the preparation of the necessary materials, then these materials began to react with one another until they turned into the new substance.

Likewise, the Exalted and Glorified Lord created the heavens and the earth by His command "Be," and these things reacted, forming the heavens and the earth.

The matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth in six days has been addressed in seven surahs of the Qur'an: four of them spoke of the creation of the heavens and the earth without mentioning what is between them, and three addressed the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. For example, in al-A'raf, Yunus, Hud and al-Hadid(1), the verses addressed the creation of the heavens and the earth only.

And in al-Furqan, al-Sajdah and Qaf(2), they spoke of the "between": so it is as if the heavens and the earth were created first as a container, then the contained was created within the container, and this is the logical order: that you prepare the container first, then place the contents in it.

As for His saying ﴿in six days﴾ (32:4): Allah addresses the Arabs with these verses, and "day" has a meaning for the Arabs linked to the movement of the sun and the moon. So how does He say ﴿in six days﴾ (32:4) when neither the sun nor the moon had yet been created?

We say: the meaning is that He created them in a period equal to six days by our reckoning now, and otherwise the day with Allah differs from our day. Did He not say, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ (22:47)? That is, in this world.

And concerning the day in the Hereafter He said: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day whose extent is fifty thousand years﴾ (70:4). So for Allah there is a measure of the day in this world and a measure of the day in the Hereafter.

The Exalted did not explain this matter of creation to us except in Surah (Fussilat), which is the one that elaborated the discourse on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and this is among the wonders of that surah.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days...﴾ (41:9–10). These are six days.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly. So He completed them as seven heavens in two days...﴾ (41:11–12). Thus the total becomes eight days.

So how do we reconcile six days in summary with eight days in detail? They said: the numbers are understood by taking their summary to mean their detail, because the detail can be added up piece by piece, whereas the summary is the final outcome.

Now repeat the verses with me:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance...﴾ (41:9–10) — and all this belongs to the requirements of the earth — ﴿in four days...﴾ (41:10), meaning that these requirements follow what came before them.

So the meaning is: within the completion of four days, the first two days being included within the four, just as if you said: I travelled from Cairo to Tanta in an hour, and to Alexandria in two hours, so the first hour is counted within those two hours.

Thus the Exalted created the earth in two days and created what is necessary for it within the completion of the four days; time is a completion of time, because an event completes an event. So the final outcome is six days, and there is no contradiction among the verses: ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ (4:82). And it is remarkable that this detail comes in (Fussilat).

As for His saying ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾ (32:4): the Exalted addresses creation with what brings things closer to their minds, because kings or holders of authority on earth do not settle on their chairs until their affair is firmly established for them.

So the meaning of ﴿istawa﴾ (32:4) is: ascended, sat and settled. All these meanings suit the verse, but within the framework of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (42:11).

Just as Allah has an existence unlike your existence, a hearing unlike your hearing, and an action unlike your action, so too He has an istiwa', but not like your istiwa'. If you enter a sitting room, for example, at the house of the town's sheikh, the mayor, the governor and the president of the republic, you will find differing levels, each according to what suits him. If humans differ in one and the same thing, shall we equate ourselves with the Creator, mighty and majestic?

So the meaning of ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾ (32:4) is: the affair of creation was firmly established for Him. ﴿For you there is not, besides Him, any protector or intercessor﴾ (32:4). The protector (al-wali) is the one who is close to you and near you, and to whom you turn in events; he is your first refuge. The intercessor (al-shafi') is the one who intercedes for you with the one who holds your affair. The protector is the one who helps you himself, whereas the intercessor mediates for you with the one who helps you. So you have no protector and no intercessor besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you call upon vanish except Him...﴾ (17:67). No one saves you and no one comes to your aid except Allah. ﴿Then will you not remember?﴾ (32:4).

It is as if this matter should always be in your mind, so that you do not neglect Allah, for you are a child of changing states, and events take turns with you, so no condition settles with you: you are between wealth and poverty, health and sickness, strength and weakness.

So always remember that you have no protector and no helper except Allah. When you keep this in mind, your heart is at rest, and why not, since you lean upon a protector and a helper who never forsakes you and never abandons you for a moment. When this feeling mingles with your heart, you face events with boldness, and when you face an event boldly, the event takes none of your strength, for the one who fears events weakens his effective power.

For example, a family man who fears death and leaves his young children without a provider: if he examined himself he would say to himself: why fear for my dependants after me? Did I create them, or do they have a Creator who watches over them and provides for them, through the faithful community, with many fathers? If he said this to himself, he would not worry about their affairs, and he would be truthful, as the one who praised said: "You flew with orphanhood to the limit of perfection."

And another said:

* The one with fathers said: "Woe to me, I have no father." *

And why not? Islam has guaranteed that orphans live under the shelter of the Muslim community in a better state than one who has a father and a mother.

So when a person knows that he has a support from a capable divinity and a lordship that does not hand him over, he meets events with strength, certainty, contentment and faith that he will never be lost as long as he has faith in a Lord. And the word "Lord" will come to his mind by compulsion in a time of hardship, when people forsake him and the means fail him, so he finds none but Allah; even if he is a disbeliever, he would say in hardship: "O Lord!"

His saying ﴿besides Him﴾ (32:4) means: there is no other. And if another is found, it is by Allah's inclination of that other toward you, for good, whatever it is, returns to Allah.

Then the Almighty, glory be to Him, says:

﴿He governs the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day whose extent is a thousand years of what you count.﴾

In this verse there is a refutation of the philosophers who said that God, exalted be He, is capable and a creator, but that He exercised His sovereignty over His dominion only once: He created the laws (al-nawamis) and the regulations, then left them to operate in the management of this universe. We say: No, rather He, glory be to Him, ﴿governs the affair﴾ [al-Sajdah], i.e., the affairs of creation, and He, glory be to Him, is the Sustainer (qayyum) over it.

Otherwise, what would be the meaning of ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾ [al-Baqarah] if what you say were true? Rather, He, glory be to Him, created the universe and manages its affairs under His own watch, may He be mighty and majestic. The proof of His sustaining His creation is that He created the causes (al-asbab) in a particular regularity. So when He wills to break this regularity with anomalies that go beyond the known laws, as He broke for Ibrahim, peace be upon him, the law of burning, and as He broke for Musa, peace be upon him, the law of the flow of water, the breaking of laws in the universe is a proof of His sustaining, and a proof that the affair of creation is still in His hand, glory be to Him.

If the matter were as the philosophers say, the universe would be like an alarm clock: you set it and then leave it to work on its own. Had that been so, the fire into which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was thrown would have been extinguished, for example.

Therefore, when one of the knowers (al-'arifin) was asked about His saying, ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾ [al-Rahman], "What is your Lord's matter now, since it is established that the pen has dried?" he said: "Matters that He manifests and does not originate; He raises some peoples and lowers others."(1)

Thus, the matter of creation is manifestation (ibda') not origination (ibtida'): the affairs of creation are prepared in advance, awaiting God's command for them to appear.

We mentioned this meaning in the interpretation of His saying, ﴿His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin]. The word ﴿says to it﴾ [Ya-Sin] indicates that this thing already exists in fact, awaiting God's saying to it: "Appear into the realm of existence."

So the Almighty ﴿governs the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾ [al-Sajdah], then the results return to Him, glory be to Him: ﴿then it ascends to Him﴾ [al-Sajdah]. God sends down to the earth, then receives from it, because the angels who carry out the affairs each have their own work and specialization. We call this, in our world, the process of follow-up among people: the head of a work assigns a group of his employees to work, then does not leave them, but follows up with them so that the work is done properly, and even holds each of them accountable according to what he deserves.

It is the angels who ascend the results to Him, glory be to Him, ﴿in a Day whose extent is a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Sajdah]. So the ascent will be by the angels, and the stride of the angels is not like your stride; therefore what humans do in a thousand years, the angels do in a day.

An example of this is what we read in the story of Sulayman, peace be upon him, when he said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ [al-Naml].

This request from Sulayman, peace be upon him, was made in the presence of an assembly of humans and jinn, but no human spoke, and none of them took up this task; rather, an 'ifrit took it up, and he was not an ordinary jinn. The 'ifrit is a skilled jinn with his own capabilities; otherwise, among the jinn there are also those who are (labkhah), who cannot do such tasks well, just as is entirely the case among humans.

The 'ifrit said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ [al-Naml]. This means it would take time, an hour or two. But the one who had knowledge from the Book said: ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾ [al-Naml], meaning: in the blink of an eye, because of the knowledge he had. Therefore, when Sulayman saw the throne settled beside him in the twinkling of an eye, he said: ﴿This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Naml].

Thus: an action takes time in proportion to the power of the doer; the greater the power, the less time it takes. We have clarified this matter in our discussion of the Night Journey and the Ascension.

As for the meaning of ﴿by what you count﴾ [al-Sajdah]: i.e., by your own years.

(1) From Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾ [al-Rahman], he said: "It is among His matters that He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises some peoples and lowers others." Al-Suyuti said in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/699): "It was narrated by al-Hasan ibn Sufyan in his Musnad, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, and Ibn 'Asakir."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Most Merciful.﴾ (32:6)

The words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿That...﴾ (32:6) refer to the governance of the affair from the heaven to the earth, then the following of the affair and its outcomes. All of this is because He, glorified is He, is ﴿the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ (32:6), and because He, glorified is He, is ﴿the Almighty, the Most Merciful﴾ (32:6). Thus the Truth, glorified is He, teaches us that the one who commands must follow up on what he has commanded.

We have said that "Knower of the unseen" means that He, by greater priority, knows the witnessed. But the Truth, glorified is He, mentioned His knowledge of the witnessed so that no one would think that Allah is unseen, knowing only the unseen. We have already explained the meaning of "witnessed" here when we discussed the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He knows what is spoken openly and what you conceal﴾ (21:110).

Al-jahr (the open, audible) or al-shahada (the witnessed) means the mixed audible, when voices overlap so that you cannot distinguish them, even though it is audible before you and witnessed. As for the Truth, glorified is He, He knows every voice and returns it to its owner. So His knowledge of the audible here is stronger than His knowledge of the unseen.

The meaning of ﴿the Almighty﴾ (32:6) is: the One who is not overcome and not subdued, so no one can turn Him away from His knowledge or from His willings in His creation. And with His might, He, glorified is He, is ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ (32:6).

Creation is bringing into existence from non-existence, with wisdom, toward a purpose and a defined mission. It is not pointless; the Creator does not make things haphazardly as they happen to come. Before He creates, Allah the Mighty and Majestic knows what He is creating and knows the mission it will perform, so He creates with specifications that achieve this purpose and fulfil this mission.

It may seem to you that some creatures have no mission in life, or that some of them could have been created in a better form than they are.

Here we mention the man who reflected on the creation of Allah and said: "It is not possible for anything to be more wondrous than what exists." And the boy who saw the blacksmith take straight iron rods, bend them and twist them, so the boy said to his father: "Why does the blacksmith not leave the iron rods straight?" The father taught him that these rods cannot perform their mission except by their bending. Consider, for example, the hook (khattaf) and the tool for gathering fruit from trees: if they were straight, they would not perform their function.

In the light of this matter we understand the Prophetic hadith in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning women: "They were created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its upper part. If you try to straighten it, you will break it, and if you leave it, it will remain crooked. So treat women kindly."(1)

When you reflect on the ribs in your chest cage, you find that they do not perform their function of protecting the heart and the lungs except in this crooked shape, which embraces the two most important organs of your body. Thus this crookedness is tenderness, compassion and protection. Likewise is the mission of woman in life: do you not see that during pregnancy, for example, she is gentle with her burden, preserves it and protects it, and when she has given birth she is even gentler and more tender toward it?

Therefore, this description from the Messenger of Allah is not an insult to women, nor a diminishing of their status, because this crookedness in the nature of woman is what completes her mission. Accordingly, we find that a woman's tenderness predominates over the evenness of her intellect, and her mission requires this nature. As for man, his intellect predominates so as to suit his mission in life, since work and the ordering of affairs under his responsibility are entrusted to him.

Therefore: Allah has created each one for a mission, and in each of us, whatever apparent deficiency he may have, there is a distinguishing feature by which he is distinguished. The man whom you see has no intellect and no cleverness, and you say: "Why did Allah create such a person?" But you see him strong of build, carrying loads and hardships that you cannot bear. And the short man, for example, you see his defect in the shortness of his stature, but another sees it as one of his merits, and perhaps employs him for this quality.

When you consider, for example, the process of education and compare the numbers of pupils in primary stage with how many reach higher education, and how many of them fall away along the way: if they all obtained advanced certificates, the situation would not be sound. Otherwise, who would fill the humble professions and crafts and other things? Therefore this disparity must exist, because one mind needs thousands to carry out its plan, and the worth of every person is what he does well, whatever his work.

Therefore we have said: no one should look down on another because he is superior to him in something; rather, let him look at what the other possesses, for the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, distributed talents among all creation. It is enough that you recite the words of the Truth, the Glorified: ﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule another people, perhaps they may be better than them...﴾ [Al-Hujurat].

So Allah, ﴿who perfected everything He created...﴾ [As-Sajdah], because every creature is prepared for a mission. Marvel at the workings of destiny in this matter: you find two brothers, one of whom works in perfumes and the other in sanitation, and you find this one content with his work and that one content with his work.

Indeed, you find people whom Allah created with some deficiency or abnormality: when one of them is content with Allah's allotment to him and His decree concerning him, he excels through this deficiency or this abnormality. Some of us have observed, for example, the one with a withered hand: when he strikes a person with that withered hand, how strong it is! And how people fear him because of his strength! And he may excel at tasks that a normal person does not excel at.

If you say: if the Creator, Glorified is He, made everything He created good, then what of disbelief? Allah created it and it still exists, so where is the goodness in it?

We say: By Allah, were it not for the tyranny of the disbelievers, people would not have loved faith; just as, were it not for the existence of injustice and unjust people, people would not have felt the taste of justice. Thus the Truth, Glorified is He, creates a thing and creates from its opposite a repellent to it.

Then He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿And He began the creation of man from clay.﴾ [As-Sajdah]. Man, whom Allah honoured above the rest of creation, was begun by Allah from clay, which is the lowest of the classes of existence. We have said that all classes end in serving man: animals, which are nearest to man, then plants, then minerals, and from minerals man was created.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic compensated for the mineral, which serves the rest of the classes, when He commanded the honoured human being to kiss it in an obligation prescribed upon him once in his lifetime, namely the obligation of Hajj: He commanded him to kiss the Black Stone and to worship Allah the Exalted through this kissing. Therefore people crowd around the Stone and fight over it, though it is a stone and they are human beings whom Allah has honoured. This is only so that arrogance in the human soul may be broken, and that no one may be haughty toward another.

We have already explained that the mischief-makers who love to find fault with the words of Allah have said: Allah, the Exalted, said in the matter of creation once ﴿from water...﴾ [Al-Mursalat], and once ﴿from dust...﴾ [Al-Kahf], and once ﴿from clay﴾ [Al-Mu'minun], and once ﴿from sounding clay...﴾ [Al-Hijr], and once ﴿from black mud altered...﴾ [Al-Hijr]... etc. So which of these elements is the origin of man?

We have said: these are different stages of one thing, and stages do not require the initial intention. Water and dust together form clay; if the clay is left until its smell changes, it is black mud altered (hama' masnun); if it is left until it dries and hardens, it is sounding clay (salsal). These elements do not contradict one another, and you may say that man was created from water, or from dust, or from clay, and so on.

What is meant here is the first man, our master Adam, peace be upon him. Then Allah made his offspring from a despised fluid (ma' mahin), and sulala (offspring/extract) is the essence of a thing. Thus the Creator, Glorified is He, created us first from clay, then made for us spouses and reproduction, from which men and women result.

Then the Creator, Glorified is He, reserves for Himself the freedom of power in this matter, as if He were saying to you: beware lest you understand that I create only through pairing; rather, I am able to create without pairing, as I created Adam; and I create from a man without a woman, as I created Eve; and I create from a woman without a man, as I created Jesus, peace be upon him.

The marital relationship may be present while Allah makes it barren, without fruit. Thus the freedom of power encompasses every kind of rational division in this matter. Read, if you wish: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females on whom He wills and bestows males on whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.﴾ [Ash-Shura].

So this is a matter of the Creator's freedom of power, Glorified is He, and it is not a "mechanical" process, because it is a gift from Allah: ﴿He bestows females on whom He wills...﴾ [Ash-Shura]. Note that Allah here mentions females first, the sex which people do not prefer to be born to them; yet you find that the one whom Allah blesses with a daughter rejoices in her, and knows that she is a gift from Allah, and Allah compensates him with a husband for her who will be more obedient to him than a son.

Likewise, if the barren person were content with his barrenness and knew that it is a gift from Allah, Allah would compensate him with the children of others, and he would feel that they are all his children. Why do we accept Allah's gift in males and in females, yet not accept barrenness, which is also Allah's gift?

Moreover, do you not see children who kill their father, and who kill their mother? Therefore the matter requires of us acceptance, submission and faith that barrenness is a gift, just as childbearing is a gift.

Furthermore, the first human, Adam, peace be upon him, who was made from clay, came from the beginning in his complete and perfect form: Allah created him as an upright man, so he was not, for example, a child who then grew up and the course of development passed over him. Rather, Allah created him in His form, that is, in the form of Adam.

Some say: Allah created Adam in His form, meaning in the form of the Truth(2). The pronoun returns to Allah, Exalted is He, and what is meant is "in the form of the Truth," not "in the reality of the Truth." Allah is Living and bestows life from His life; Allah is Powerful and bestows power from His power; Allah is Rich and bestows richness from His richness; Allah is Knowing and bestows knowledge from His knowledge.

Therefore it has been said: "Take on the characteristics of Allah," because He, Glorified is He, has bestowed upon you attributes from among the attributes of His manifestation. He has given you these attributes, so give the attribute within you its distinction and take on its character. For example: be strong against the wrongdoer and humble and gentle toward the wronged, in accordance with the saying of Allah Exalted concerning the attributes of the believers:

﴿Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves...﴾ [Al-Fath].

And He said: ﴿Humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers...﴾ [Al-Ma'idah].

These contrasting attributes are combined in the believer, because he does not have a single nature; rather, the situation and the responsibility are what dye him and turn him toward the suitable attribute.

We have said that scholars of analysis, in their practice, have proven the truth of the Qur'an in this reality, namely the creation of man from clay, when they found that the elements constituting the human body are the very elements present in the soil, and their number is 16, the strongest being oxygen, then carbon, then hydrogen, then nitrogen, then sodium, then magnesium, then potassium, etc.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 32, verse 8:

Al-nasl (offspring) is the descendants and progeny, and al-sulalah (lineage, essence) is the essence of a thing, extracted from it as a sword is drawn from its scabbard. Thus al-sulalah is the finest part of a thing. For this reason we say: "So-and-so is of the lineage of such-and-such," and "So-and-so is the scion of glory" (sakhil al-majd), meaning in a context of praise. Even with horses, they preserve known, pure lineages for them and register birth certificates that establish the purity of their lineage.

This offspring and this lineage, God created them from water, which is the man's semen and the woman's ovum.

God described this water as ﴿mahin﴾ [al-Sajdah] (contemptible, base) because it passes through the channel of urine and goes its way if it does not reach the womb. In this contemptible water there are wonders. May God have mercy on al-Aqqad(1) who said: the fundamental particles of the entire world could be placed in half a sewing thimble. Consider how much a man ejaculates in a single time from this quantity! So the matter is the precision of formation and the greatness of the Creator, for in this simple particle are the characteristics of a complete human being: it carries his color, his sex, his attributes, and so on.

We have already said, regarding the world of the particles (alam al-dharr), that in each of us there is a particle and a living cell from our father Adam, peace be upon him.

Then He says, may He be exalted:

﴿Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts; little are you grateful.﴾

This proportioning was first for the first human being whom God created from clay, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him﴾ [al-Hijr]. Adam (peace be upon him) passed through the stages mentioned in this proportioning, and likewise is the matter with his offspring: the Creator, mighty and majestic, proportions them and they pass through these same stages: from a drop (nutfah), then from a clinging clot (alaqah), then from a lump of flesh (mudghah)... etc., then the spirit is breathed into him.

And if man did not witness how he was created, God, exalted is He, makes what we witness a proof of what is hidden from us. If we did not witness creation, we have witnessed death, and death is the undoing of life and of creation. It is known that the undoing of a thing comes in the reverse order of its building. So if we wanted, for example, to demolish a building of several floors, the last floor built is the first floor demolished.

Likewise in death: the first thing in it is the departure of the spirit, which was the last thing in creation. When the spirit departs, the body stiffens, or as they say (shaddhab), and this stage is similar to the stage of clay (salsal); then it becomes putrid and its smell changes, as it was in the stage of black mud (hama' masnun); then this body decomposes and what is in it of moisture evaporates, and some elements remain which turn into dust, so that it returns to its first origin.

So: take from what you see a proof of the truthfulness of your Lord, mighty and majestic, regarding what He has told you of the creation which you did not witness.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And made for you hearing and sight and hearts...﴾ [as-Sajdah], we have previously discussed these organs. The scholars of physiology have established the function of each organ and limb, and when each limb begins performing its function. They have proven that the ear is the first organ to perform its function in the infant, as evidence: if you place your finger before the eye of a baby after its birth, it does not blink, whereas it startles if you make a sound beside it. That is because it hears immediately after birth, while sight is delayed from three to ten days.

Therefore the sense of hearing is the one that accompanies a person, and its function does not end even in sleep, and through it one is awakened, whereas the eye does not work during sleep.

God, exalted is He, explained this matter in the story of the People of the Cave: when God willed to put the People of the Cave to sleep for this long period, and the cave lies in a desert with the sounds of winds, storms and wild animals, God struck over their ears and deadened this faculty in them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So We struck over their ears in the cave for a number of years﴾ [al-Kahf].

So: the ear is the first of the organs to perform its function, then the eye, then the rest of the organs, and the last to function are the nerves. This is evident from the fact that a child's temperature may reach forty degrees, for example, and we see him running and playing without feeling anything. Why? Because his nervous system has not yet matured, so he does not feel this heat.

Therefore we always find the Qur'an placing hearing before sight, and sight comes before it only in one verse, His saying: ﴿We have seen and heard...﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12], because it depicts a scene of the scenes of the Resurrection, in which the disbelievers are surprised by the terrors of the Resurrection, and the sight overwhelms them before they hear the voice when the caller calls.

Among the marvels of Qur'anic eloquence is that the word for hearing (asmaa') corresponds to sight (absaar), but what is mentioned here is ﴿the hearing and the sights...﴾ [as-Sajdah: 9]. So "hearing" is singular and "sights" is plural. Why was hearing made singular and sight plural?

They said: because the ear has no covering that blocks sounds from it, whereas the eye has a covering (eyelid) that is drawn over it and prevents visible things from reaching it. So it is one hearing for me, for you and for everyone: everyone hears one sound, whereas visible things are many, so what you see may not be what I see.

Sight does not come singular in this context except in one place, His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hearing and the sight and the heart—about all of these one will be questioned﴾ [al-Isra': 36]. That is because the verse speaks of responsibility, and responsibility is individual and cannot be transferred, so it must be singular.

It is appropriate that God mentions hearing, sight and hearts after speaking of the matter of creation, because man is born from his mother's womb knowing nothing, and through these organs and senses he learns and acquires information and experience, as He said: ﴿And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts, that you may be grateful﴾ [an-Nahl: 78].

So: these organs are necessary for the existence of man as God's vicegerent on earth, and through them he coexists with others, and he must acquire information, otherwise how would he coexist with his environment?

We have said that in order for man to learn he must use these perceiving senses, each in its own domain: the tongue in speech, the eye in sight, the ear in hearing, the nose in smell, and the fingertips in touch.

We have also said that these senses are the mothers of the known senses, since we later came to know other senses. Therefore the scholars, anticipating this development, named these known senses "the apparent senses" (al-hawass al-zaahirah). Afterwards we came to know the sense of "bayn" by which we know the fineness and thickness of cloth, and the sense of "adal" (muscular sense) by which we know weight.

So: when a person is born he needs these senses to coexist, to perceive, and to interact with the society in which he lives. Had a person lived alone, he would not need, for example, to speak; but by his nature he lives with the group, so he must speak to communicate with them, and before that he must hear in order to learn speech.

We have previously said that language is the offspring of hearing: a child born in an Arab environment speaks Arabic, one who lives in an English environment speaks English, and so on. What the ear hears, the tongue relates; if the ear does not hear, the tongue does not speak.

Therefore we said earlier in Surah al-Baqarah, in His saying: ﴿Deaf, dumb...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18], that muteness, which is the absence of speech, results from deafness, which is the absence of hearing. So hearing is the first function of man, and it gives me the first foundation in my life with the society around me.

It is known that learning to read, for example, requires a teacher whose pronunciation I hear: this is alif, this is ba', this is fatha, this is damma... etc. If I do not hear, I cannot pronounce correctly, and I cannot write.

Through hearing the message is conveyed from God from heaven to earth; therefore hearing is mentioned before sight.

And when the Exalted spoke about hearing in this manner, He said: I will hear the names of things: this is earth, and this is sky... etc. Therefore when we teach a pupil we say to him: this is an eye, and this is an ear.

After the pupil learns reading from his teacher, he can then read on his own, and he needs the faculty of sight for the task of reading. When he completes his teaching and is able to correct his reading himself, and the information he acquired through his hearing and sight has matured in him, he can read other things than what his teacher read to him, and he can cultivate and educate himself until a scholarly faculty forms in him through which he innovates new things that perhaps his teacher does not know. This is the task of the heart (fu'ad): ﴿and made for you hearing and sight and hearts...﴾ [as-Sajdah: 9].

Meanings are gathered through these senses until a person becomes sound, possessing the faculty by which he learns, and then he teaches others.

Spoken language is learned only through hearing: I heard from my father, my father heard from his father, and you can trace this chain back until it reaches Adam (peace be upon him), father of all mankind. If you say: from whom did Adam hear? We say: he heard from God when He taught him all the names: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them, then presented them to the angels and said: Tell Me the names of these, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 31].

This is a logical matter, because audible language cannot be invented by anyone. Nevertheless, some object to this point, saying: this means language is tawqifi (divinely revealed), with no role for us in it, in the sense that we do not introduce anything new into it.

We say: yes, language is a matter of tawqif, but God gave Adam the names and taught him them, and with these names he can agree upon the naming of other things for the information that arises in his life.

Otherwise, how would we have named "radio" and "television" etc., which are all новинки that necessarily need names, and a name exists only after its referent exists? This is the task of the language academies, which decide these names and approve their use. The academy has agreed to name the telephone "masra" (هاتف: musra), and television "tilfaz", etc.

So: we brought these words and agreed upon them, because they express the meanings we want, and these words are the offspring of the names Adam (peace be upon him) learned. Thus language began as tawqifi and ended as wad'i (conventional).

As for His saying, exalted is He, after these blessings: ﴿little are you grateful﴾ [as-Sajdah: 9], it is evidence that these blessings require gratitude, but few of us are grateful. We ought to thank the Bestower whenever we hear, whenever we see, and whenever our minds work and reach something new.

Therefore the believer's gratitude to his Lord does not end, just as his festivities and joy do not end. For example, we rejoice on the day of 'Id al-Fitr at our breaking of the fast and our performance of the worship God has enjoined upon us. On 'Id al-Adha we rejoice, because our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) bore on our behalf the ransom through his son, so that all of us would be spared from each one ransoming himself by slaughtering his son to draw near to God; otherwise the matter would have been burdensome for us. Therefore we rejoice on 'Id al-Adha, slaughter the sacrificial animals, and perform the rites of the Hajj.

And since the believer ought to rejoice in performing the obligations and doing acts of obedience, why do we not rejoice whenever we pray, fast, or pay zakat? Why do we not rejoice when we obey God by doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden? Why do we not rejoice in this world until the day of the greatest joy comes, the day when the fruit of these deeds is gathered and we receive their reward, Paradise and its bliss?

And if you wish, read your Lord's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—their Lord guides them by their faith; rivers flow beneath them in Gardens of Bliss. Their call therein will be: "Glory be to You, O God," and their greeting therein is "Peace," and the last of their call is: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Yunus: 9–10].
