Meaning of ﴿We have strayed into the earth...﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:10]: that is, we have disappeared into it, and our particles have dispersed, such that we do not know where they went or into what they were transformed, into an animal or into a plant? When this happens, ﴿Shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:10], meaning: will God create us anew, once again?

And the Exalted One responds to them: ﴿Nay, but they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:10]. Bal (nay, rather) indicates a turning away from their previous statement and the establishing of another reality, namely that they do not deny the Resurrection and the gathering, but rather they deny the meeting with God. ﴿Nay, but they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:10], because the matter of the gathering is impossible for them to deny, since the proof for it is clear.

As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation? Nay, but they are in doubt about a new creation﴾ [Qaf 50:15]. The One who created from nothing at first is capable of restoring from what exists, because your particles and your raw materials exist, so restoration is easier than beginning. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:27].

So then: their denial is not of the Resurrection in itself, but of the meeting with God and of the reckoning. But they deny the Resurrection because it leads to the meeting with God, and they dislike the meeting with God, so they deny the matter from its very beginning.

1 ʿayiya ʿan al-amr yaʿya: he was unable to undertake it. So His words ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?﴾ [Qaf 50:15] mean: We were not wearied and did not fail in the first creation, and likewise We will not be unable for the second creation on the Day of Resurrection. This is a proof of the possibility of resurrection after death, for whoever is able to create the first time is able, all the more so, to create a second time. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/46].

Here you notice that they are speaking about resurrection, ﴿And they say, "When we have gone astray in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ (32:10). It is known that resurrection is the bringing into being of life, yet the Qur'an speaks to them of death, which is the undoing of life, in order to remind them of this truth.

The meaning of ﴿He will take you (yatawaffakum)﴾ (32:11) is from *tawaffaytu dayn min al-madin* (I received the full debt from the debtor), that is, I took it in full, without deficiency. The intended meaning here is death. The verb *tawaffa* (to take in full) is attributed sometimes to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ (39:42).

It is attributed to the Angel of Death: ﴿Say, "The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you."﴾ (32:11). It is attributed to his assistants among the angels: ﴿until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail in their duty﴾ (6:61).

This is because the supreme matter of death is in the hand of the Creator, glorified be He. He alone is the Giver of life, and He alone has authority over undoing it and removing it from its possessor. Therefore Allah forbade killing and made the killer cursed, because he demolishes the structure of Allah. When Allah decrees death for a person, He permits the Angel of Death to carry it out, and he is 'Azra'il (Azrael).

So this matter has three stages: the taking (tawaffi) is from Allah, who commands 'Azra'il; then 'Azra'il commands the angels entrusted with this matter; then the angels carry out the command.

Consider the word ﴿Our messengers took him (tawaffathu rusulunā)﴾ (6:61). That is, they took him in full. He did not say "they annihilated him," for example. Therefore we say, "his soul was seized," meaning it went to where it had been before it was breathed into him; it went to the Higher Assembly. Then the body dissolved and returned to its origin and melted into the earth, a part here and a part there, as they said, ﴿"When we have gone astray in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ (32:10).

The one who is taken in full has not been annihilated; rather he exists in complete existence, his soul and his body, and Allah is able to restore him on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore He did not say "We annihilated him." This matter also resolves for us a difficulty in the story of our master Jesus, peace be upon him, for Allah said concerning him: ﴿When Allah said, "O Jesus, I will take you in full (mutawaffīka) and raise you to Me"﴾ (3:55).

Some say that he, peace be upon him, died first and then Allah raised him to Himself. The correct view is that the conjunction *wāw* here indicates mere joining, so it implies neither sequence nor immediate succession. If you wish, read the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus the son of Mary﴾ (33:7).

The address here is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Noah is before him, peace be upon him.

The meaning here is that Allah, exalted be He, placed the taking in full before the raising, so that no one would suppose that Jesus, peace be upon him, was exempt from death. He therefore put first the thing about which there is doubt or dispute. Since Allah has taken him in full, He has taken him without deficiency, and this means that he was not crucified and was not killed; rather Allah raised him to Himself in full.

As for His saying, ﴿Say, "The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you"﴾ (32:11), it came as a reply to their saying, ﴿"When we have gone astray in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ (32:10). The Truth who said, "I created man," did not say, "I will annihilate him," but "I will take him in full." He is with Me complete with his soul and his constituent particles, and He who created at the beginning is able to restore, and to gather the particles that were scattered.

As for His saying about the Angel of Death, ﴿who has been entrusted with you﴾ (32:11), that is, he watches over you and does not neglect you; he stays with you and does not turn away from you, so that there is no escape from him and no release, as the people of gnosis (ahl al-ma'rifa) said: "Death is an arrow released toward you in action, and your lifespan is the measure of its journey to you. It is certain to happen, just as we said about a calamity (muṣība), that it was only named a calamity because it will befall you without fail."

As for His saying, ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ (32:11), that is, on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 32, verse 12:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain."﴾ (32:12)

This verse presents us with a scene from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which the criminal is driven in humiliation to what he deserves of punishment. It is as if you see a criminal, for example, being led by the police, shackled in chains, tasting humiliation and disgrace, so your soul is healed when you see him receive his recompense after he has wearied the world and troubled people.

In this scene, the Truthful, glorified is He, addresses His Prophet ﷺ, who is the first addressee, and then it becomes an address to his nation: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord...﴾ (32:12). That is, in the state of their existence, they are hanging their heads. The estimated response of the conditional clause is: "You would have seen a wondrous matter that would heal your chest from what they did to you."

In this style we note the precision of expression in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only you could see...﴾ (32:12). He did not say, for example, "If only you knew," because God's report is as if it were the vision of the eye. When God informs you of a matter, know that it is more truthful than your eye when you see, because your eye may deceive you, but God's report to you is the truth.

The meaning of ﴿hang their heads﴾ (32:12): the naks (نكس) is making the higher lower, and the head in a human being is always the highest thing in him.

This root has occurred in His saying concerning the story of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he smashed the idols and hung the axe on their chief: ﴿Then they were turned back upon their heads [and said], "You have already known that these do not speak."﴾ (21:65)

So after they had returned to their senses and accused themselves of wrongdoing, they relapsed and returned to their falsehood, saying: ﴿You have already known that these do not speak.﴾ (21:65)

This word also occurs in His saying: ﴿And whoever We grant long life We reverse in creation; so will they not reason?﴾ (36:68)

The meaning is: We return him from the state of strength and youth to the state of weakness, decrepitude and inability, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing.﴾ (16:70)

So after strength he leans on a staff, then he cannot walk, so he crawls, or he is carried as a small child is carried. This is the reversal in creation. When we reflect upon it, we say: Praise be to God, that He has spared us from this period and this reversal. And we know that death is a kindness from God and a mercy to the servants. Do you not see that one who reaches this stage is a burden to his family, and they may wish for his death so that he may rest and they may rest?

The hanging of the criminals' heads contains an indication that this is the outcome, so beware of opposition. Whoever is arrogant and haughty in this world will have his head lowered in the Hereafter, and whoever is humble before God in this world will have his head raised. This is the meaning of the noble hadith: "Whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him."(1)

In the hanging of the criminals' heads on the Day of Resurrection there is another meaning, because the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, will deal with every transgressor in the Hereafter in the same kind as what he did in this world, and these whom God caused to hang their heads in the Hereafter did that in this world. Read, if you wish, your Lord's saying: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to hide from Him.﴾ (11:5)

That is, they lower their heads so that they do not confront the Messenger of God. For truth has a force and power before which falsehood cannot stand. Therefore we hear from the people of truth: "Come, confront me, give me your eye in your eye." The people of falsehood must be shamed and must shrink from confrontation, because it is not in their interest.

This inability to confront drives a person to commit the most heinous crimes, and it leads him to killing. Killing does not indicate strength; rather it indicates incapacity, weakness and cowardice in facing confrontation. The killer acknowledges that he cannot face his enemy's life, so he kills him; had he been strong, he would have confronted his life.

Among the punishments that come in the same kind as what a person did in this world is God's saying concerning those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of God: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the cause of God – give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day it is heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs are branded with it, [and it will be said], "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ (9:34–35)

Glory be to God, it is as if it were an exact image of what they did in this world. One of them is approached by a beggar and frowns in his face, then turns away from him; he turns his side to him, then turns away and turns his back to him. The punishment comes with this very same detail. So the intelligent person must beware of these transgressions, for from their kind will be the punishment in the Hereafter.

As for these criminals in the state of their hanging heads, they say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾ (32:12). This is their speech, yet the Qur'an did not say, "They said: we have seen and heard"; the omission of the verb here indicates that the saying is not easy for them, because it is an acknowledgment of their first error, out of the humiliation of repentance.

We have said that this is the only verse in which sight is placed before hearing, because when the Hour comes with its terrors, we see the terror first, then we hear what we see.

Therefore He, exalted is He, portrays the effect of this terror: ﴿And you see the people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of God is severe.﴾ (22:2)

In the course of our previous discussion of the faculties—hearing, sight and the heart—we failed to mention an important verse that came in a different order, which is God's saying: ﴿God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil; and for them is a great punishment.﴾ (2:7)

Here the heart came first, and the heart was combined with hearing in the seal because they share it, while sight was singled out for another thing, namely the veil covering their sights. That is because the previous verse about hearing, sight and the heart was a bestowal from God, so it began with hearing, then sight, then it ascended in bestowal to the heart. But here the context is one of stripping these blessings, so the most important is stripped first: he brought the heart, then hearing, then the sights.

But what did they see, and what did they hear, in their saying ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾ (32:12)? The first thing the disbeliever sees on the Day of Resurrection is ﴿God is with him﴾ (24:39), alone, glorified is He, with no partner from among the partners they worshipped in this world, and they have no protector apart from Him, no intercessor, and no helper.

The meaning of ﴿we have heard﴾ (32:12) is: what You sent down, O Lord, to Your Messenger, and we bear witness that it is the truth, and we affirm the Messenger in conveying from You, and that he is not a fabricator, nor a poet, nor a sorcerer, nor a liar.(3)

But what is the benefit of this acknowledgment now? And how will it benefit them while they are in the abode of reckoning, not in the abode of action and obligation? And how similar this acknowledgment is to the acknowledgment of Pharaoh before he drowned: {I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel have believed...} (10:90). Therefore God answered him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.﴾ (10:91)

So their saying ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾ (32:12) is an acknowledgment from them that they were in error, and that they desire to return to the right course, as He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteous work in what I have left behind."﴾ (23:99–100), and God answered him: ﴿No! It is but a word he is saying.﴾ (23:100)

Then He revealed the reality of their situation: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars.﴾ (6:28)

Here they say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain.﴾ (32:12). But will certainty occur in this situation? Certainty occurs through the unseen matter, whereas you now are in sensory, witnessed certainty, so it is a certainty that will not avail.(5)

(1) Abu Nu'aym narrated in Hilyat al-Awliya' (8/46), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him." And likewise (7/129), from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "O people, be humble, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Whoever humbles himself before God, God raises him.'"

(2) Meaning: He covered it and firmly secured its covering, so they do not understand and do not hear. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/187]. Abu Ishaq said: the meaning of khatama and taba' in the language is one, namely covering a thing and making certain that nothing enters it. [Lisan al-Arab, root: kh-t-m]

(3) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5353): "That is, we saw what we used to deny, and heard from what we used to reject. It was also said: we saw the truth of Your threat, and heard the confirmation of Your messengers."

(4) Qatadah said: They saw when sight did not benefit them, and they heard when hearing did not benefit them. [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/544, attributing it to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]

(5) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5354): "It was said: the meaning of ﴿we are certain﴾ (32:12) is: the doubts have now departed from us. They used to hear and see in the world, but they did not reflect, and they were like one who neither sees nor hears. So when they became alert in the Hereafter, they became as though they had heard and seen."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 32, verse 13:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾

Here someone may ask: Why did Allah make people believers and disbelievers, obedient and disobedient? Why did He not make us all guided and obedient? Is this difficult for Allah, glory be to Him? No, it is not difficult for Allah, the Exalted, as evidenced by the fact that He created the angels obedient, carrying out His commands, glory be to Him: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [At-Tahrim].

Likewise the earth, the heavens, the mountains, and so on, all of them glorify Allah and worship Him: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification...﴾ [An-Nur, 41].

And He said: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ [Al-Isra, 44]. Then Allah, the Exalted, gives some of His creation the knowledge of this glorification, as He said concerning Dawud (peace be upon him): ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with Dawud...﴾ [Al-Anbiya, 79].

Yes, they also glorify with other than Dawud, but the distinction is that they share with him in one glorification, as if they were a (chorus) reciting one anthem.

We know from the story of the hoopoe and Sulayman (peace be upon him) that he knew the matter of tawhid in its most complete form, as the best of people in faith in Allah, and it is he who said of Bilqis, the queen of Sheba: ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided﴾ [An-Naml, 24].

And he said: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden (al-khab') in the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare?﴾ [An-Naml, 25].

When the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wishes to demonstrate His power to His creation, He makes weakness into strength and strength into weakness. Look at the state of the early believers, how humiliated and oppressed they were, and when they embraced Islam, Allah raised them through Islam and made them masters.

Famous is the story of the Companion Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, when the oppressed ones such as Ammar and Bilal were admitted to him, and he left the chieftains of Quraysh at the door. His father rebuked him for this: how can slaves enter while these masters are left at the door? Abu Bakr said: "O my father, Islam has raised up the lowly. If these have had their noses lifted in pride that slaves should enter before them, how will it be with them when Allah admits them into Paradise before them?"

It is remarkable that this statement should come from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, given what is known of his gentleness, tenderness of heart, and forbearance.

This is a form of the changing of conditions and the convergence of opposites. The Truth, blessed and exalted, addressed this matter in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they winked at one another﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin, 29-30], meaning: they mocked them and ridiculed them, as we hear people of falsehood say to the upright person, "Lower your wing for us."

Would that the matter ended there. Rather, when they returned to their families, they repeated this mockery, boasted of it, and rejoiced in harming the people of piety and uprightness: ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as guardians over them﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin, 31-33]. But the Truth, glory be to Him, ends this situation with His saying: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon the couches, looking on﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin, 34-35]. Then Allah asks them: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin, 36].

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: Let no one think that any of My creatures has defied Me. Rather, I willed for them to have choice, then I informed them of what I love for them to do. Allah wills to have knowledge of occurrence concerning the one who believes in Him, while he had the power not to believe. Otherwise He, glory be to Him, has known from eternity, so that the act may be proof against its doers. Therefore: beware lest you think that by your choice you have broken the subjugation of the Most High.

We have previously said: those who have grown accustomed to rebelling against Allah while claiming faith in Him, who disbelieve and rebel against His obedience and disobey Him... We say to them: since you have become accustomed to rebelling against the commands of Allah, why do you not rebel against sickness, for example, or against death? Thus: you are a slave in spite of your noses.

Here He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance...﴾ [As-Sajda, 13], meaning: We would have made people like the angels and like the compelled creatures that have no choice. We have previously said that all creatures were offered the choice in bearing the trust, not man alone. But the difference is that the son of Adam took choice in detail, while the rest of creation took choice in summary, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer and ignorant﴾ [Al-Ahzab, 72].

The meaning of guidance in ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance...﴾ [As-Sajda, 13] is the guidance of assistance (hudā al-ma'ūnah). Otherwise, Allah has granted all people the guidance of indication (hudā al-dalālah) to the path of good. So whoever takes hold of the guidance of indication and says "upon the eye and the head" receives the guidance of assistance, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad, 17].

To understand the difference between the two guidances, read: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them...﴾ [Fussilat, 17], meaning: We showed them and directed them, ﴿but they preferred blindness over guidance...﴾ [Fussilat, 17].

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [As-Sajda, 13].

The Truth, glory be to Him, wishes to establish for His creation that He is the most worthy of wisdom in creation, as evidenced by the fact that whoever deviates from Allah's will must corrupt society through it, as we see societies suffer through the disbelief of the disbeliever and the disobedience of the disobedient.

The Truth, glory be to Him, leaves the disbeliever to disbelieve by his choice and the disobedient to disobey by his choice, so as to harm people through the sin of the disbeliever and the sin of the disobedient. Then they return to the legislation of Allah and seek refuge at His threshold, glory be to Him. Had people acted by the law of Allah, no corruption in the universe nor any disorder in their lives would ever have occurred.

Therefore we rejoice when Allah takes vengeance on the people of disbelief and the people of disobedience, and we say: "Praise be to Allah who has relieved the lands and their people of them."

So: opposing the method of Allah at its peak is disbelief in Him, glory be to Him, and in other matters is disobedience to His command. It is this that shows the merits of faith and the sweetness of legislation. We have said that legislation must be taken by the one who is obligated in its entirety, with what is for him and what is against him. Allah obligated you not to steal from people, and He obligated all people not to steal from you.

The meaning of ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect...﴾ [As-Sajda, 13] is: it occurred, was established, and was decided. This meaning comes with the word "precede," as in: ﴿And certainly Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers﴾ [As-Saffat, 171], and in the story of Nuh (peace be upon him): ﴿So load into it from every pair two, and your family, except those against whom the word has preceded...﴾ [Al-Mu'minun, 27].

And Allah said, relating the words of the disbelievers in their dispute on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us; indeed, we will taste [the punishment]﴾ [As-Saffat, 31].

As for the meaning of ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together﴾ [As-Sajda, 13]: we know that Allah created Paradise and created people to fill it, and created Hell and created people to fill it. There is no shortage of places in them. Paradise was prepared to hold all creation if they believe, and likewise Hell was prepared to hold all creation if they disbelieve.

Therefore, when the people of Paradise go to Paradise, they inherit the places of the people of Hell in it (2), as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And they will be called out, "This is Paradise, which you have inherited for what you used to do."﴾ [Al-A'raf, 43].

And "al-jinna" means: the jinn and the ghouls.

1 Al-khab': everything that is hidden; it is every concealed, veiled thing. The khab' in the heavens is rain, and on the earth it is plants. [Lisan al-Arab, root: kh-b-a]

2 Ibn Majah transmitted in his Sunan (4341) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one of you but he has two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. When he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling; and that is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾ [Al-Mu'minun, 10]." Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: its chain is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 32, verse 14:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

﴿So taste (fa-dhuqu) [the consequence] of your forgetting the meeting of this your Day. Indeed, We have forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity (al-khuld) for what you used to do.﴾ (32:14)

The implied meaning is: taste the punishment, as in another verse: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar (Hell).﴾ (54:48). This is said to the leaders and heads of disbelief: ﴿Taste it! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble.﴾ (44:49).

He chose the sense of taste because every means of perception may be connected to some kind of luxury in life, whereas tasting is connected to the sustenance of life, which is eating and drinking, and by them the human being's life is sustained. They are two necessities of life, not mere luxuries in it.

In another place, Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) shows us the effect of being made to taste, saying of the town that disbelieved in its Lord: ﴿So Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾ (16:112). Picture hunger as a garment that takes hold of the whole body, as if Allah, exalted is He, wants to show us the bite of hunger, which is not confined to the belly alone but extends to all the limbs. So He said ﴿the garment of hunger...﴾ (16:112) to encompass the tasting, as though every limb of the body will taste the pain of hunger. This meaning is conveyed only by the wording that the Qur'an has chosen.

The poet was also alert to this comprehensiveness that takes hold of the whole body, when he spoke of divine love when it rises in the heart and overflows from it to encompass all the limbs. He said:

The flashes of Your remembrance stir up my affection,
so I feel their stirring in my heart.
No limb of mine is without its longing (sabaabah),
as though my limbs had been made into hearts.

The reason for this tasting is ﴿for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day...﴾ (32:14), i.e., the Day of Resurrection, about which We told you and warned you of its terrors. We did not seize you unawares; rather, We alerted you to the evil outcome, so there is no excuse for you now. We magnified these terrors for you, so it was obligatory for you to heed them, to take warning from them, and to verify their truth.

As for the believers, when they see this terror and this punishment descending upon the disbelievers and deniers, they rejoice, because Allah has saved them through their faith from this punishment.

The consequence of forgetting the meeting with Allah is ﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you...﴾ (32:14). You forgot the meeting with Allah, you forgot His directives, and you neglected His warning and admonition to you. We have left you not in neglect, but We have left you from the extension of mercy toward you. My mercy used to encompass you in the world, and I did not reserve it for those who believe in Me; rather, I made it for the believer and the disbeliever alike.

Thus everything in existence gives the human being, simply as a human, so long as he takes the means, with no difference between believer and disbeliever. This is in this world. But in the Hereafter, We will forget you from this mercy, which you do not deserve, and instead: ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.﴾ (32:14).

If you rebelled against Allah and disbelieved in Him in a limited world, whose life-span in it is limited, then the punishment that befalls you today is everlasting and permanent. Your loss is great and your calamity is grievous.

We have said that working in this world for the Hereafter represents an equation that must be solved correctly. Your life in this world is not measured by its duration, but by the period of your stay in it, which is a limited life span, whereas the Hereafter is an endless eternity. If the bliss in both were equal, the extension of time would make the Hereafter preponderant.

Moreover, your bliss in this world is according to the extent of your capabilities and your movement within it, whereas the bliss of the Hereafter is according to the capabilities of Allah in the universe. The bliss of this world either escapes you or you escape it, but the bliss of the Hereafter remains and never escapes you, because you are eternal in it.

So this is a transaction that must be calculated correctly, one for which it is worth selling this world with all its precious and costly things. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called it a profitable trade.

Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) said of the disbelievers: ﴿Those are the ones who bought error in exchange for guidance, so their trade did not profit, nor were they guided.﴾ (2:16).

1 al-Sababah: longing. And al-sabb: the lover, the one who yearns. [Lisan al-Arab, root: s-b-b]

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.﴾

Al-khurur (falling down): falling without order or arrangement, as in His saying: ﴿So the roof fell down on them from above them...﴾ [An-Nahl: 26]. In another place, with the same meaning, He says: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration﴾ [Al-Isra: 107], that is, before the Qur'an, ﴿and they say, "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled."﴾ [Al-Isra: 107-108].

So al-khurur is to descend toward the ground in prostration without deliberation, and every prostration in the Qur'an that accompanies this root (kharra) is evidence that it has become a disposition and an automatic reflex in the believer. Indeed, the Truth, glory be to Him, confirms it with His saying: ﴿They fall down upon their faces in prostration﴾ [Al-Isra: 107], because it is a prostration that takes hold of the chin, so he is firmly established in humility. It is beyond the prostration we know in prayer, upon the seven known members.

Al-khurur is not mentioned together with ruku' (bowing) except in one place, which is His saying concerning our master Dawud: ﴿And Dawud realized that We had tested him, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness and fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24].

In another place He says: ﴿And they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility﴾ [Al-Isra: 109]. Thus, whenever they increase in humility, they increase in submission. It is as if they have fallen in love with obligation and loved the commands of Allah, and therefore they went to great lengths in humility and servitude to Allah, the Exalted. This matter explains to us the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so increase in supplication."(1)

In prostration you place your face and forehead, which are a symbol of height and elevation, upon the ground, in submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

1 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (482), Book of Prayer, and likewise Ahmad in his Musnad (2/421), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 32, verse 16:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says about them:

﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend of what We have provided them.﴾ The word tajafi means abandonment (tark), but abandonment may be accompanied by longing and by pain, as when you bid farewell to a beloved and leave him while you are not indifferent to him and have not come to hate him (qala). As for jufa, it is abandonment out of aversion to what is abandoned. So these believers who forsake their beds are as though their sides dislike the bed and shun it, because they leave it for a more lasting and greater pleasure, which is the pleasure of union with Allah and of intimate conversation with Him.

Here we should mention that Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when he went to bury Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah be pleased with her, stood at the grave of the Messenger of Allah and said: "Peace be upon you, O my master, O Messenger of Allah. My patience has grown weak for your chosen one, and my endurance has diminished for her. Yet in consoling myself over your great separation and your grievous calamity there is a place of consolation: the one who bore your loss, O Messenger of Allah, finds every other loss easy after you. Indeed, I laid you, O Messenger of Allah, in the hollow of your grave, and your soul departed between my chest and my throat. My night is sleepless and my sorrow is everlasting, until Allah chooses for me the abode in which you dwell. This, and your daughter will inform you of the state of your community and of their conspiracy to oppress her, so ask her closely and inquire of her condition. This, and the time since you have gone is not long, and your remembrance has not left us."

Then, when he wished to turn away from the grave of his beloved, he said: "And peace be upon you, a peace of one who bids farewell, neither weary nor tired. If I depart, it is not out of weariness, and if I remain, it is not out of ill opinion regarding what Allah has promised His patient servants."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds...﴾ means: they dislike them and shun them, although they are the dearest thing a person leans upon for rest. When life stirs in a person and he has strength and vigor to work in life, work is a branch of the existence of life. By strength he walks, and by strength he carries loads.

When the load weighs on him, he sets it down from himself to rest, but he can walk without a load. If walking tires him, he stands; if standing tires him, he sits. Therefore it happens that you say to your companion: "Please, carry this load for me," and he says: "O shaykh, am I able to carry myself?"

So: the fatigue in this case arises from the weight of the body on the two feet, so standing tires him. Do you not see that if the imam prolongs the prayer, for example, we shift our weight between the feet, once on this one and once on that one? As for sitting, it relieves a person, because it widens the area bearing the body, so the weight of the body in sitting is distributed over the whole buttock. If the fatigue reaches a point where sitting tires him, he lies on his side and stretches his whole body on the ground, so the weight is distributed over all the limbs, and no limb bears anything but its own weight.

If after all this a person feels fatigue, he turns onto his other side or onto his back. All of these are kinds of rest for the human body. But he does not attain complete rest except when he sinks into sleep, and they call this succession muscular sequences.

The proof that sleep is complete rest is that in it you do not feel the pain you feel when awake, if you are suffering from an illness, for example. These are all stages that the believer passes through, and so when he dies he rests even more, and then when he is resurrected on the Day of Resurrection he rests the greatest rest. They are stages we pass through until we are cast into the embrace of our Creator, mighty and majestic.

So: the bed is the last stage of wakefulness, and it comes only after several stages of fatigue. Nevertheless, the believers' longing for their Lord and their desire to stand before Him, glorified is He, makes them forget this rest and makes them indifferent to it, so they shun it in order to stand before Allah.

In another place He, exalted is He, said about them: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ [adh-Dhariyat]. Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿calling upon their Lord...﴾ [as-Sajdah], meaning: they call upon their Lord while in a state of fatigue, as though mere supplication refreshes them. Why, and yet they have not been answered yet? They said: because they place their needs and requests with One who is able to bring them to pass. Furthermore, the sweetness of their meeting with their Lord in prayer makes them forget the fatigue they suffer.

And the believers call upon their Lord ﴿in fear and hope...﴾ [as-Sajdah], meaning: fear of what has happened from them of shortcoming in the right of Allah, and that they have not offered to Allah, exalted is He, what is due of piety and obedience. ﴿And hope...﴾ [as-Sajdah], meaning: for forgiveness. ﴿And they spend of what We have provided them﴾ [as-Sajdah], and what is meant here is zakat.

Therefore, in His saying: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds...﴾ [as-Sajdah], we see that this forsaking was for the purpose of prayer, because the Qur'an customarily pairs prayer with zakat, so after it He said: ﴿and they spend of what We have provided them﴾ [as-Sajdah].

1 Occasion of revelation of the verse: al-Bazzar (2250, Kashf al-Astar of al-Haythami) narrated from Bilal ibn Rabah that he said: "We used to sit in a gathering, and some of the Companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him, would pray between maghrib and 'isha', so this verse was revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds...﴾ [as-Sajdah]." al-Suyuti cited it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 136), attributed it to al-Bazzar, and weakened it through his shaykh Abdullah ibn Shayb.
2 Qalaytuhu (qala): I hated him and detested him to the utmost degree, so I abandoned him. Qala means hatred. [Lisan al-Arab, root q-l-y]
3 As-sahr: the lungs and the heart; that is, she died while leaning against his chest. An-nahr: the chest, which is the place of the necklace on it. [Lisan al-Arab]
4 As-sarmad: the lasting of time, whether night or day; and sarmad is that which is perpetual and does not cease. [Lisan al-Arab, root s-r-m-d]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 32, verse 17:

We have said that the Truth, glorified is He, has concealed the secrets of goodness from creation, and has given them of it only in proportion to their need for it. So when He, glorified is He, wishes to reward His believing servants, He does not reward them with what they know of the goods of this world and its capabilities within it; rather He rewards them with what He, glorified is He, knows, and with what is commensurate with the capabilities of His power.

We cannot express these capabilities, because the words of language cannot express them. It is well known that a person does not assign a name except when the named thing and its meaning are found first. Therefore, when speaking about this bliss, the Most High said: ﴿So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes⦆ [al-Sajdah 17].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said about Paradise: "In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." (1) So how do we name these things, and how do we imagine them when they are beyond our perception? Therefore we shall be surprised by them when we see them, God willing.

Then, do you not see that when the Truth, glorified is He, presents to us a portion of the mention of Paradise, He does not say to us "Paradise is such and such"; rather He says: ﴿A description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised⦆ [al-Ra'd 35]. That is to say: what We present to you is not Paradise, but something resembling it. As for it in reality, it is beyond the description that language can convey. So I give you an image close to your minds.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, purifies the likeness He presents to us from its blemishes in this world. Consider the saying of God the Most High about the bliss of Paradise: ﴿The likeness of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered⦆ [Muhammad 15]. Among them, the defect of water was that it would become foul and change in jars, so God purified it from this defect.

Likewise in ﴿and rivers of milk whose taste does not change⦆ [Muhammad 15]. The Arab, when he traveled with milk, it would turn sour, and he would loathe it. ﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers⦆ [Muhammad 15]. The defect of the wine of this world is that it seizes the intellect and takes it away, and there is no pleasure in drinking it. Therefore we see its drinker, God forbid, gulping it down at once and pouring it into his mouth, which is evidence that it is not good. Have you ever seen a drinker of wine sipping it slowly as one sips a cup of juice, and feeling the pleasure of drinking it?

God has described the wine of the Hereafter with His saying: ﴿Neither will there be in it intoxication (2), nor will they be drained thereby (3)⦆ [al-Saffat 47].

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and rivers of purified honey⦆ [Muhammad 15]. He described the honey as purified, because the defect of honey among them was what would stick to it of pebbles and impurities as it flowed down from the beehives in the mountains. So God purified the honey of the Hereafter from the impurities of honey in this world.

However far the luxury and bliss of life may reach us, and however greatly our capabilities in this world may grow, we will never see in it a river of wine, or of milk, or of honey. Moreover, these rivers flow in Paradise without banks, and some of them even intermingle with one another without any one of them overwhelming the other. This is the boundless freedom of power.

So: when the Truth, glorified is He, explains to us the bliss of Paradise, and describes it, He gives us the likeness, not the reality, and then purifies this likeness from what mars it in this world.

Among this is that the Arab loved the lote tree, that is, the sidr (nabq), so he would shelter in its shade and eat its fruit, but what disturbed this pleasure for him was its thorns, which must hurt whoever plucks its fruit. So when God the Most High mentioned it in the bliss of Paradise, He said of it: ﴿among lote-trees thornless⦆ [al-Waqi'ah 28], that is, with its thorns removed, so enjoyment of it is complete and nothing spoils it.

When He spoke about the women of Paradise, the Most High said about the dark-eyed maidens (hur 'in): ﴿Untouched before them by man or jinn⦆ [al-Rahman 74]. Thus He negated from them what would spoil a man's enjoyment of a woman's beauty in this world, and He assured you that they are virgins whom no one has looked upon before you.

For this reason, the Most High said of the bliss of Paradise: ﴿So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes⦆ [al-Sajdah 17]. The qurrah and qarar mean stillness, and from it comes qarra fi al-makan, meaning he settled in the place. The meaning is that a person does not settle in a place except when he finds in it his comfort and the foundations of his life. So if you want to settle in a place, or buy an apartment for example, you ask about the utilities and services, such as water, electricity, roads, and so on.

Even in our colloquial expressions, and in the countryside which preserves for us the characteristics of pure nature that the falsity of civilizations and the adornment of the city have not tainted, and these natural things attract souls and draw them. The proof is that the civilized person, however high he rises, and however he lives in skyscrapers, and however all the luxuries of life are available to him, there will inevitably come a day when he takes refuge in the embrace of nature, and his soul finds no rest and settles only in the countryside, where he spends several days, where his soul is calmed there and rests from the noise of the city. Some call it the "weekend".

So the meaning of "comfort of the eye" (qurrat al-'ayn) is its settling upon a thing such that it does not turn from it to anything else. The eye does not settle upon a thing except when it pleases it and sees in it all the enjoyment it yearns for.

Among this is our saying "so-and-so's eye is full" meaning he needs no more sights than what he sees; and "so-and-so's eye is empty" meaning he is not content with what he sees, but seeks more, looking here and there.

In Paradise, the eyes are comforted such that they no longer have aspirations, for its meanings are complete, so it does not befit them to desire anything else except permanence.

For this reason God addresses His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have given pairs of them to enjoy, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein⦆ [Ta-Ha 131].

So the person whose eye is empty appears to you as one whose eyes wander, looking here and there; but if his eye were "full," it would stop there.

Among the meanings of the root (q-r-r) is al-qarr, which is intense cold, and this meaning is used as a metaphor for the joy of the soul. So a "cool eye" means a joyful one, while a "hot eye" is a sorrowful, pained one.

Among the other meanings of qarur al-'ayn is its stillness and its not moving due to illness or blindness. Among this is the saying of the woman who entered upon the caliph and said: "May God comfort your eye (aqarra Allahu 'aynaka) and complete His favor upon you." The attendees understood that she was supplicating for him, so he said: "By God, she did not supplicate for me; rather she supplicated against me." She meant "aqarra Allahu 'aynaka," that is, "may He make it still so it does not move," and "wa atamma 'alayka ni'matahu," that is, "may He remove it, for when a favor is completed it departs, and after completion there is nothing but decline."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, explains this bliss which He has concealed for His believing servants in Paradise by saying that it is ﴿a reward for what they used to do⦆ [al-Sajdah 17]. This has stirred a battle among the scholars, the battle of the beloveds: one group said that the believer enters Paradise by his deeds, as this verse states, meaning Paradise is by justice, not by grace. Another group said: rather he enters Paradise by the grace of God, as the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, indicates: ﴿Say: "By the bounty of God and His mercy, so in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate"⦆ [Yunus 58].

And the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy." (7)

When this battle grew heated, they wanted to unify these two opinions and reconcile them. They said: God the Most High has preceded the accountable person with goodness, creating for him the foundations of his life before he existed, then leaving him to delight in His favors without demanding anything of him until he reached the age of accountability.

So when God imposes obligation upon him after His prior favor upon him, it is incumbent upon him to obey this obligation as a recompense for the prior goodness of God toward him, the first goodness. Thus the reward in the Hereafter is not for the deed; rather it is pure grace from God upon His servants.

So: when you perform what your Lord has obligated upon you, it is as if you are repaying your Lord with obedience for His prior goodness toward you; and so Paradise and its bliss are an increase and grace from God. God, glorified is He, has grace upon you in the first, and He has grace upon you in the Hereafter.

Then, when the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, legislates for you and imposes obligation upon you, His legislation and obligation are in themselves grace. Do you not see that the good deed with Him, glorified is He, is rewarded tenfold, and that it is multiplied many times over, and we are His possession, glorified is He; He gives us or does not give us?

Some people of knowledge and ecstatic utterance say: God has first bestowed goodness, so it is incumbent upon the servant to bring goodness as a return for goodness, for ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?⦆ [al-Rahman 60].

And when the servant does good in obligation, his Lord revives him with another goodness, so the servant responds to his Lord's goodness toward him with goodness, and thus goodness continues between the servant and his Lord without end.

(1) Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2824), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/466), and Abu Nu'aym in Hilyat al-Awliya' (2/262), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.
(2) al-Ghawl: headache. It is said: intoxication. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-ghawl is that it seizes their intellects. [Lisan al-Arab, root gh-w-l]
(3) Anzafa al-qawm: their drink ran out. And anzafa al-qawm when the water of their well went away and was cut off [Lisan al-Arab, root n-z-f]. al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: wine has four qualities: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination; so God mentioned the wine of Paradise and exonerated it from these qualities. [Quoted by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 4/7]
(4) al-Sidr: the lote tree. Sidr among trees is of two kinds: one is wild, whose fruit is not benefited from, and its fruit does not pass easily down the throat; the second grows on water, and its fruit, nabq, is yellow and bitter. [Lisan al-Arab, root s-d-r]. al-Makhdud: that which has had its thorns removed, so there are no thorns in it.
(5) Tamathat al-mar'ah: she menstruated, so she is tamith. And al-tamth: deflowering, which is intercourse with bleeding. So the meaning of "lam yatmithhunna insun" is: no one has touched them.
