(7) A hadith agreed upon. Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6463), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (2816), from Abu Hurayrah.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Is then he who was a believer like him who was a wicked transgressor? They are not equal.﴾ (18)

First, we note in the wording that "mu'minan" (believer) and "fasiqan" (wicked transgressor) are in the singular form, so the analogical expectation would be to say "la yastawiyan" (they two are not equal). Yet the Qur'an's context is ﴿لَّا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾ (they are not equal), and we have already said that the relative particles "man" and "ma" (who/whoever) may refer to the singular, the dual, or the plural, and to the masculine or the feminine. Sometimes the context attends to their wording, and sometimes it attends to their meaning.

The meaning here: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًا﴾ — the Almighty is not speaking of a single individual but of a group, or else it was said in response to a specific situation between a believer and a disbeliever, and Allah wished to give it generality rather than restrict it to the particular occasion. So the context attended to the particular occasion in "believer" and "disbeliever," and attended to the general subject in ﴿لَّا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾. The jurisprudential rule states that what counts in the Qur'an is the generality of the wording, not the particularity of the occasion of revelation (2).

It is said that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt when he disputed with 'Ali (may Allah honour his face). He said to him: "I am younger than you in youth, stronger than you in vigour, more eloquent than you in tongue, sharper than you in spear-thrust, braver than you in heart, and fuller than you in ranks." 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, answered him with what refutes and nullifies all of this, and said to him: "Be silent, O wicked one, for there is no excellence for a transgressor."

The meaning: if you are as you say, then you have squandered all of this through your wickedness, since you have employed the strength of your youth, your vigour, the sharpness of your tongue, and the courage of your heart in falsehood, in disobedience, and in barring from the way of Allah.

Thus the verse combines the particularity of this occasion in ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًا﴾ with the generality of the subject in ﴿لَّا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾, so this ruling extends to the plural as well.

The words ﴿لَّا يَسْتَوُونَ﴾ come as if they were the answer to the question ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًا﴾. But why did the answer not come as, for example: "The believer and the wicked transgressor are not equal"? They said: because this style is called the style of emphatic persuasion, in which you make the opponent himself pronounce the judgment.

It is like when a friend says to you: "You went through a crisis and did not stand by me." You could say to him: "I stood by you on such-and-such day and such-and-such day," as a plain statement from you. But a plain statement from you may be true or false, so you resort to another style, with which he cannot deny and can only acknowledge your favour, and you say in the form of a question: "Did I not provide you with such-and-such on such-and-such day?" You only ask him once you are confident that his answer must come in accordance with your intent, and then his words become a proof against him.

Therefore the Almighty put this matter in the form of a question: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًا﴾. And we must say, in answer to this question: a believer and a wicked transgressor are not equal, and whoever says this has agreed with the intent of his Lord.

(1) Occasion of revelation: Al-Wahidi and Ibn 'Asakir reported through Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-Walid ibn 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt said: "I am sharper than you in spear-point, more expansive than you in tongue, and more able to fill the ranks of the battalion than you." 'Ali said to him: "Be silent, for you are only a wicked one," and so this verse was revealed: ﴿Is then he who was a believer like him who was a wicked transgressor? They are not equal.﴾ [Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Suyuti, p. 136].

(2) "The majority of scholars hold that what counts is the generality of the wording and not the particularity of the occasion, so the ruling derived from a general wording extends beyond the specific case of the occasion to its counterparts, such as the verses of li'an, which were revealed concerning Hilal ibn Umayya's accusation of his wife, yet the ruling derived from this general wording includes ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ (6) [al-Nur] beyond the incident of Hilal, without need of another proof." [Mabahith fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an, Manna' al-Qattan, p. 80, Maktabat Wahba, 1988].

(3) Al-Jald: strength, vigour, and patience [Lisan al-'Arab, root j-l-d].

(4) Dhariba al-lisan: one whose tongue is sharp. Al-dharib: sharp in anything [Lisan al-'Arab, root dh-r-b].

Since the believer and the defiant sinner are not alike, each of them receives a recompense suited to them: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of refuge as a lodging, because of what they used to do.﴾

Although the word "believer" (mu'min) came in the singular, this verse makes clear that the intended meaning is the plural, that is, generality, because it has taken what was singular and made it plural. This is evidence that this singular noun, in its category, comprises a great many. Compare the saying of the Exalted: ﴿By time (1), indeed mankind is in loss (2)﴾ — so "mankind" (al-insan) is singular, from which the plural is excepted: ﴿except those who believed and did righteous deeds (3)﴾, because the word "mankind" here denotes a group. The "al" in it is the "al" of comprehensiveness (al-istighraqiyyah).

So the Truth, glorified is He, moves us from the believer to generality, ﴿As for those who believed...(19)﴾, and from the defiant sinner to ﴿And as for those who defied...(20)﴾. These are two opposing groups, each having its suitable recompense:

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of refuge...(19)﴾. The "ma'wa" (refuge) is the place to which a person retreats and seeks shelter to protect him from every harm, as the Exalted said concerning Jesus and his mother Mary, peace be upon them both: ﴿And We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of settlement and running water (50)﴾ — meaning, they could settle there, because it has the necessities of life. ("Ma'in") means: a spring of water.

Among that is the saying of the Exalted about the son of Noah when he said to his father: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water...(43)﴾. His father warned him and cautioned him, so he said: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for whom He has mercy...(43)﴾.

In this story we notice the tenderness of fatherhood from our master Noah when he said ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family...(45)﴾. But his Lord, mighty and majestic, does not leave him upon this matter; rather He corrects it for him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose work was other than righteous...(46)﴾.

Thus, sonship here is not sonship of lineage but sonship of faith and deed. Do you not see that the Messenger of Allah said to Salman al-Farisi, who was not of the Arabs at all: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House" (1).

And although lineage benefits from fathers to sons, this is not a privilege of the prophets alone; it is for all people, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds...(21)﴾ [al-Tur].

The joining of children to their fathers is in reality an honour for the fathers, that they find their children with them in Paradise as a reward for the fathers' faith and righteous deeds. If the children are below the age of obligation, it is natural that they be joined to their fathers; indeed their rank will be greater than their fathers' rank, because children who die before maturity have no fixed places, but rather roam freely in Paradise, playing as they wish.

We have illustrated this with a small child whom you take along on a visit to one of your friends: you sit in the sitting room, while the small child runs throughout the house and enters any place in it that no one prevents him from entering. Therefore they call children the "da'amis" (playful darters) of Paradise (2).

Here some raise the question that a person is held hostage by his deed and does not benefit from the deeds of others; each is hung by his "irqub" (Achilles' tendon), as we say. Some ask: why do we pray over the dead, when the prayer over him is not of his own deed? If the prayer over him has a benefit that returns to him, then he has benefited from something other than his deed; and if it has no benefit, then it is futility, and far be it from Allah to legislate something futile.

We say: Have you prayed over every dead person, whether a believer or a disbeliever? No, we pray only over the believer. So your prayer over him is a result of his faith, and a part of his deed, and had it not been for his faith we would not have prayed over him.

Returning to the meaning of the word "ma'wa" (refuge): Paradise is the refuge of the believer, protecting him from the Fire and its horrors. ﴿As a lodging (nuzulan) for what they used to do (19)﴾ — meaning, a recompense for their righteous deeds. A "nuzul" is the place prepared for a guest who arrives upon you to lodge in; therefore they call a hotel a "nuzl". If the luxurious hotels we see now are what humans have prepared for humans, then what about what the Lord of humans has prepared for His righteous servants?

1 On the authority of 'Amr ibn 'Awf al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marked out the trench in the year of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), from the sand-hill of al-Samar, at the edge of the land of Bani Harithah, when the ink was reached; then he cut forty cubits, between every ten. The Muhajirun and the Ansar disputed over Salman al-Farisi, and he was a strong man. The Ansar said: "Salman is one of us." And the Muhajirun said: "Salman is one of us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/418), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (3/598), and al-Dhahabi weakened its chain because of Kathir ibn 'Abd Allah.

2 On the authority of Abu Hassan, who said: I said to Abu Hurayrah: "Two of my sons have died; so will you narrate to me from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a hadith by which our souls may be comforted concerning our dead?" He said: "Yes. 'Their young are the da'amis of Paradise; one of them meets his father – or he said his parents – and takes hold of his garment, as I take hold of the hem of this garment of yours, and he does not stop until Allah admits him and his father into Paradise." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2635), and similarly Ahmad in his Musnad (2/477, 510).

﴿So they defied...﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:20]. From the root fisq (moral deviance), which means "going out," as in "the date (balah) has defied," meaning it came out of its skin. Here it refers to those who went out of obedience to God and out of what the Truth, glory be to Him, requires.

﴿...their refuge is the Fire...﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:20]. We have said that a refuge (ma'wa) is the place to which one retreats and which protects one from every harm, so how is the Fire described with it here?

They said: the refuge is the place where a person settles according to his own desire and his own manner, whereas these people are lodged there against their will. Or the speech here is based on prior mockery and derision, as in His saying: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:21].

It is well known that good tidings are only given with something pleasing, and similarly: ﴿Taste, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [ad-Dukhan 44:49]. This is frequent in the style of the Qur'an, because it is a style that pains the disbelievers and diminishes their standing.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, portrays for us the despair in which the people of the Fire are: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:20]. In another place He said of them: ﴿They will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ [az-Zukhruf 43:77]. So there is no hope for them of getting out, nor even of death which would relieve them of what they are in. Rather, the angels turn them back into the punishment and say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:20].

So the "tasting" (al-idhaqah) has passed beyond the tongue and taken hold of all the limbs, so that every atom of them tastes the punishment of the Fire as recompense for what they used to deny in the world, since they denied the foundation, which is the return to God on the Day of Resurrection.

Then, the punishment of the wicked is not confined to the punishment of the Hereafter; rather, they will have another punishment which they taste in this world:

﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment (1) short of the greater punishment, so that they may return.﴾ (32:21)

﴿The lesser punishment..﴾ (32:21): i.e., the near one, meaning in this world. ﴿Short of the greater punishment..﴾ (32:21): i.e., the punishment of the Hereafter. This punishment that will befall them in this world is one of the manifestations of Allah's mercy, even toward the disbelievers and the wicked, because Allah, exalted is He, gave the reason for it in His saying: ﴿so that they may return﴾ (32:21).

So, what is meant is the punishment that reaches them in the abode of responsibility (dar al-taklif), such as captivity, humiliation and disgrace at the hands of the great number and strength of the believers. Did not 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (2), despite his well-known slightness of body, mount Abu Jahl in one of the battles, throw him to the ground and trample him with his foot? It is related that Abu Jahl looked at him in this state and said: "You have climbed a difficult height, O shepherd of the goats!" (4)

The punishment in the Hereafter is described as "the greater punishment" because it is the all-encompassing punishment from which there is no escape and no refuge.

His saying, glorified is He, ﴿so that they may return﴾ (32:21): i.e., in hope that they will return to the courtyard of faith. We have said that "la'alla" (so that/perhaps) expresses a certain hope when the action is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; but the hope here is a hope regarding the servant who possesses choice, and therefore some of them returned, while others did not.

(1) Ibn 'Abbas said: by "the lesser punishment" he means the calamities of this world, its diseases, afflictions and what befalls its people, with which Allah tests His servants so that they may repent to Him. The like of this was related from many others. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Mujahid and Abu 'Ubayda said it means the punishment of the grave. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/462].

(2) He is 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ibn Ghafil al-Hudhali, one of the great Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in virtue, intellect and closeness to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was the first to recite the Qur'an aloud in Makkah. He was very short, such that those sitting would almost hide him. He was in charge of the treasury of Kufa after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), then he came to Madinah in the caliphate of 'Uthman and died there at about sixty years of age.

(3) 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba said: Ibn Mas'ud was a thin, short man. Ibrahim al-Taymi said: Ibn Mas'ud climbed a tree and they began to laugh at the thinness of his shins, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you laughing at them? They are heavier in the scale than Mount Uhud." [Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra 3/143].

(4) This was at the Battle of Badr, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered his Companions to search for Abu Jahl among the slain. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud passed by Abu Jahl and found him at his last breath, so he placed his foot on his neck and said to him: "Has Allah disgraced you, O enemy of Allah?" Abu Jahl said to him: "You have climbed a difficult height, O shepherd of the goats!" Then Ibn Mas'ud cut off his head. [Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham 2/276, 277].

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.﴾ (22)

Here too, our Lord, blessed and exalted, presents this matter to us in the form of this affirmative question, as if He, glory be to Him, is saying to us: "I have taken your acknowledgment, O My servants, so tell Me: is there anyone more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turned away from them?" The natural logic is that we say: "No one is more unjust than this." This is our affirmation of this truth, and therefore the Almighty presented it in the form of a question instead of as a statement.

The meaning of ﴿was reminded﴾ [al-Sajdah] (20) is that the messages of God to His creation are nothing but a reminder of the ancient covenant of faith that God took from His servants when He said, glory be to Him: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'raf] (172). We have already said that in each of us there is a spark that witnessed this covenant, and each of us must preserve the radiance of this spark within himself by nourishing it with what is lawful, and by training it in obedience, so that the lights of faith may remain within him.

As the Exalted said: ﴿And by the soul and He who proportioned it (7), and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness (8), he has succeeded who purifies it (9), and he has failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams] (10).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 32, verse 23:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, so do not be in doubt about meeting him. And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.﴾ (32:23)

Giving (al-iytha') varies. There are those who are given a method, or a miracle, or both together. There is also a giving of a book that is limited in time, for a limited period, to a limited people, and another giving that is for all times and all places.

As for ﴿the Book﴾ (32:23), it means the Torah. ﴿So do not be in doubt﴾ (32:23) means: do not be in doubt. ﴿About meeting him﴾ (32:23): is it the meeting with Moses, peace be upon him, or the meeting with the Book? If it is the meeting with Moses, then it is good news that Allah will bring together our master, the Messenger of Allah, while he is alive according to the law of the living, and Moses, peace be upon him, who is dead according to the law of the dead. This cannot be realised unless the narration of the Night Journey and Ascension (al-Isra' wa'l-Mi'raj) is true in that the two met in it (1).

For this reason, there is a verse in the Qur'an at which we should pause and reflect attentively, which is His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ (43:45).

This is a command from Allah the Exalted to Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to ask the messengers. So when does he ask them? This verse indicates that they must meet. So this verse concerns the meeting with Moses, and the other concerns the meeting of all the messengers (2). Therefore, we must believe in the narration of the Night Journey and Ascension, and that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gathered with his brothers among the prophets, led them in prayer, and a dialogue took place between them.

But if the meaning of ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾ (32:23) is the meeting with the Book, then the Torah, as we have said, has suffered distortion and alteration, and additions and falsehoods were introduced into it. But there will come to you, O Muhammad, from the People of the Torah, the likes of Abdullah ibn Salam, who know the Torah without distortion and recount it to you secretly. These are the ones of whom Allah said: ﴿Among the People of the Scripture is an upright community; they recite the verses of Allah during the night and they prostrate.﴾ (3:113).

Did Abdullah ibn Salam (3) not confront his people, the Jews, saying to them: "How do you deny Muhammad, when you used to seek victory through him over those who disbelieved, saying to them: 'A prophet is about to appear, whom we will follow, and we will slay you with him the slaying of 'Ad and Iram' (4)? You gathered from the various lands that oppressed you and came to Yathrib awaiting the arrival of this prophet. Why then do you deny him?"

The Qur'an said of them: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it.﴾ (2:89).

Among the meeting with the Book that was promised to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is what is related from Abdullah ibn Salam: when he wished to believe, he came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander (bahт), meaning they boast of lying. If I become Muslim, they will say about me what is not in me. So ask them about me, O Messenger of Allah, before I announce my Islam." When the Jews gathered, the Messenger of Allah asked them: "What do you say about Ibn Salam?" They said: "Our master and the son of our master, our rabbi and the son of our rabbi..." Abdullah said: "Since they have said what they have said, O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah." They said: "Our worst and the son of our worst."

Abdullah said: "Did I not tell you, O Messenger of Allah, that they are a people of slander (5)?"

As for His saying ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾ (32:23), it means: We made the Book a guidance. This is evidence that among them there are those who are guided, by the evidence of the Qur'an's testimony concerning them: ﴿Among the People of the Scripture is an upright community; they recite the verses of Allah during the night and they prostrate﴾ (3:113).

His saying in the following verse:

﴿And We made from among them leaders who guide by Our command when they were patient, and they were certain of Our signs.﴾ (32:24)

1. On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Did you see the night I was taken on the Night Journey? Moses ibn 'Imran was a man, tawny, tall, with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah, and I saw 'Isa, a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair." Related by Qatadah from Abu'l-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, who said: he meant the night of the Isra'. Cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/463).
2. This is a statement of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam in the interpretation of the verse (43:45), meaning: ask them on the night of the Isra', for the prophets, peace be upon them, were gathered for him. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/129].
3. He is 'Abdullah ibn Salam ibn al-Harith al-Isra'ili, Abu Yusuf. He embraced Islam when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Madinah, and his name was "al-Husayn." He witnessed with 'Umar the conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis and al-Jabiyah, and when the strife broke out between 'Ali and Mu'awiyah he took a wooden sword and withdrew from it, and remained in Madinah until he died in the year 43 AH. [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 4/90].
4. From elders of the Ansar who said: We had subjugated them by force for ages in the Jahiliyyah, while we were people of polytheism and they were people of the Book. They would say: a prophet is about to be sent now, we will follow him, his time has drawn near, and we will slay you with him the slaying of 'Ad and Iram. But when Allah sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him. Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (1/124), citing Ibn Ishaq.
5. After 'Abd Allah ibn Salam had embraced Islam, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander, so ask them about me before they learn of my Islam." The Jews came, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "What sort of man is Abdullah ibn Salam among you?" They said: "The best of us and the son of the best of us, and the most excellent of us and the son of the most excellent of us." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "What do you think if Abdullah ibn Salam becomes Muslim?" They said: "May Allah protect him from that." He repeated it to them, and they gave the same answer. Then Abdullah came out to them and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3938), and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/108, 271, 272).

Imamah: The intended meaning of imamah (leadership) here is not temporal authority over people; rather, it is the imamah of exemplary guidance by the command of Allah. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿They guide by Our command⁠﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24]. They do not act in anything except upon guidance from Allah.

In Surah al-Anbiya' He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah; and they were worshippers of Us⁠﴾ [al-Anbiya': 73].

Al-Iqan (certainty): It is the faith that is not shaken, and does not surface to the intellect to be examined anew. That is to say, the matter has become one accepted as settled, firmly established in the soul.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 32, verse 25:

You notice in the style of the verse that it did not say, for example, "Indeed your Lord separates between them." Rather, it used the separate pronoun (huwa) to convey emphasis and exclusivity, so the meaning is: no one separates between them on the Day of Resurrection except Allah, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [Ghafir]

So, huwa comes to cut off any doubt about the existence of another.

You may also reflect on this pronoun in these verses, and on when the style uses it. The Exalted says, regarding the story of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him:

﴿Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [ash-Shu'ara'] — i.e., the idols — ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me. And who gives me food and drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me. And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara']

He used the pronoun that indicates exclusivity in guidance, feeding, giving drink, and healing, since these actions are ones someone might claim for himself. As for giving life and causing death, these belong to Allah alone, and no one can claim them, so they came without this emphasis, as it is a matter accepted about Allah, the Exalted.

Doubt arises in the matter of separation on the Day of Resurrection, because Allah the Exalted has appointed from the angels those who arrange affairs (al-mudabbirat amran) to manage the affairs of creation, and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him who protect him by the command of Allah﴾ [ar-Ra'd], i.e., following the command of Allah concerning him. So some may understand that the angels have a role in separating people on the Day of Resurrection, just as they have a task in this world.

Note here that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the term of lordship (rububiyyah), saying ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾ [as-Sajdah] and did not say "Indeed Allah." Lordship, as we have said, means provision and nurture, and it is as if He, glorified is He, is saying: be reassured, for the One who will take charge of the matter of separation is your Lord.

And His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ [as-Sajdah] is because separation only occurs over a dispute, and a dispute must be about a matter requiring the ruling of a judge to be referred to.

1 Lahu mu'aqqibat: i.e., guardian angels who follow him, protect him, and count his deeds. Or the meaning: the angels succeed one another by night and by day. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/29].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 32, verse 26:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have they not been guided to how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk? Indeed, in that are signs. Will they not then listen?﴾ (26)

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has spoken about the message with which He sent His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in order to establish in people a higher belief, which is the belief in the existence of the One God who has no partner. Then He explained that we have another meeting with Allah when this transient world ends, and then we receive an eternal life, either to Paradise, God willing, or to the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, presents His signs in the universe, He presents them so that it becomes established that He is the One who created these wondrous signs. He, glory be to Him, has not left us to look and then turn away; rather He draws our attention and alerts us to the obligation of looking at His signs in the universe. When someone comes who wants to alert your intellect, know that he does not want to deceive you or catch you unawares. Your Lord says to you: receive this My speech with the utmost reflection, remembrance and reasoning.

Had he not been confident that by reflection, reasoning and remembrance he would reach the goal he desires, he would not have alerted your intellect to His signs, just as you see the seller of a good commodity, confident of its quality, displaying it to you, uncovering it for you, and inviting you to examine it and consider what is in it. He does this only because of his confidence in his merchandise and that it will earn your satisfaction.

As for the seller of adulterated goods, he deceives you and adopts methods of evasion, circling around and deluding. For instance, when you go to buy a shoe and it is tight, he says to you: it will loosen after you walk in it; and if it comes out loose, he says: shall I bring you a larger one? In order to make you think it is tight. The methods of such people are obvious and hidden from no one. Whoever wants to cheat or deceive twists the matters to conceal them from your reflective, remembering and considering intellect.

As for the Truth, glory be to Him, He often said in His Qur'an: "Will they not listen?", "Will they not reason?", "Will they not reflect upon the Qur'an?" Therefore it is in the interest of the call that people reason about it and reflect upon it, whereas some adherents of other religions, when you debate with them, say: keep reason away from this matter. Why? Because he is confident that if it were examined by reason, reason would reject it and not accept it. The Truth, glory be to Him, wants to leave no excuse for anyone in conveying the message; the call has reached everyone with a sound and clear delivery. Those are the signs of Allah in the universe.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, brings miraculous signs to establish the truthfulness of the Messenger, making them contrary to the laws of the universe in that in which the people excelled, in order to cut off their argument. Then He brings the rulings that convey the method with "do" and "do not," and He makes clear that the soundness of the movement of life lies in applying this method, and He leaves the violations to reveal some defects. So when you look at a defect or a blemish in society, you know that it is a natural result of opposing the method of God; it is as if the violation itself confirms the ruling.

Then He, glory be to Him, makes clear that He sent many messengers from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, because the human being, who is His vicegerent on earth, is afflicted with heedlessness when he becomes immersed in the causes of the world, and it takes over all his thought and all his concern, so he forgets what God asked of him. It is the habit of man not to remember except what benefits him immediately.

Therefore we find that many people forget what others owe them, and remember what they owe others.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, says: I have left My creatures with no proof against Me, for I have scattered before them the striking signs of the universe, which are clear signs that no one has claimed for himself. Despite the multitude of atheists and disbelievers, we have never seen anyone claim to have created the sun or the moon, nor has anyone said: I drive the wind, or I cause the crops to grow, or I send down water from the clouds.

The Truth, glory be to Him, also alerts us: do not forget, O human, that you are a vicegerent of God on earth, and beware lest you think you are original in it; for at the moment you think you are original in this world, God abandons you and leaves you to yourself, and you perish, as happened to Qarun when God expanded provision for him in the world, so he became arrogant with what was in his hand and thought it came from his own effort, knowledge and labour.

The outcome was ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home.﴾ (81) [al-Qasas], to alert all people that wealth is not the property of its owner; rather he is made a trustee over it, and had it been his own wealth he would have guarded it. Thus the Truth returns people through events to the nature of the primordial fitra of vicegerency, because the corruption of the universe comes from regarding man himself as original in the universe.

We have said before: if a person looks at the universe with a careful, fair and penetrating look, he will know what follows: that everything in which the hand of man has not interfered is sound and performs its task in the most perfect manner, and that every corruption in the universe is only from man's interference in it without the law of his Lord; and if he had interfered in it by the law of his Lord, the things in which he interfered would have been set right for him, just as the things in which he did not interfere were set right.

And we have said: when you see a defect in the universe, know that it is the result of a right of God that has been neglected. When you see a poor person dying of hunger, or a naked person who has nothing to cover his nakedness, know that the wealthy have fallen short in fulfilling God's right in zakat, for God, exalted is He, prescribed it with precise reckoning; had the capable person paid the zakat due on his wealth, no one in the society around him would remain in need.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, wants us to preserve within our souls the faith of the fitra, and the first atom of faith which desire has not entered and forgetfulness has not mixed with. This atom witnessed the first covenant in which Allah said:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] – lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."﴾ (172) [al-A'raf].

That is: before the desires of the world seize you and make you forget, so that you deny this testimony and say: ﴿"Indeed, we were of this unaware" (172) or [lest] you say, "It was only that our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ (173) [al-A'raf].

Whoever preserves this atom, and this divine touch which God placed in him with His own hand, and the covenant which God took from him, the light of this fitra remains with him, and this illumination keeps blazing within him; but if he neglects it, sins and heedlessness obliterate it.

Therefore the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gives us the example, saying: "The trust (i.e., the voluntary obligations from Allah) is presented upon hearts like a reed mat, strand by strand. Whatever heart absorbs it, a white spot is marked upon it; and whatever heart rejects it, a black spot is marked upon it, until there are two kinds of hearts: a white one like smooth stone, which no trial harms as long as the heavens and earth endure, and a black one, dusky, like an overturned cup, which knows no good and denies no evil." (2)

So acts of obedience or sins accumulate upon the heart just as the strands of a reed mat are arranged one beside another; the heart whitens with acts of obedience, or blackens with sins. A human being has matter and spirit; the spirit within matter gives it life, movement, understanding, thought and action, and both, before they joined, were glorifying God, the Exalted; everything in existence glorifies Him: ﴿Each knows its prayer and its glorification.﴾ (41) [al-Nur].

The human being must understand this reality and preserve the faithful nature in his atoms and components so that they remain radiant and luminous with the light of faith. If he neglects this nature, changes occur and disharmony arises among the atoms of the human self. When your will drives the body and the soul into disobedience, your body hates you and your soul hates you, because you have opposed the method of its Creator, mighty and majestic is He; it glorifies and worships while you are heedless, disobedient and sinful. Therefore your soul curses you and your limbs curse you.

Among the mercies of Allah toward the disobedient is that he sleeps, so his limbs rest and his soul rests from his sins and takes its ease in worshipping its Lord, where it has no contender and no opponent from its owner's will. Therefore a person feels rest on sleep and rises from it energetic, because of the harmony and balance that occurred among the atoms of his self during sleep.

It is narrated that our master, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his eye would sleep while his heart did not sleep (3), because his limbs were always in harmony, in his sleep and in his waking. So if you see a person overcome by exhaustion of strength, know that he has tired out his atoms, and they wish to be rid of him through sleep, as if they say to him: sleep, for you are no longer fit to coexist with me.

In sum: the Truth, glory be to Him, always alerts us from this heedlessness through the messengers; then He, glory be to Him, leaves for the earlier messages evidence that supports the messengers present and helps them perform their mission. Therefore He says to us: look at the messengers who came before, and how the end of those who denied them was.

﴿Have they not been guided to how many generations We destroyed before them...﴾ (26) [as-Sajdah], as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been created in the lands, and Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?﴾ (6-10) [al-Fajr].

Thus these pyramids to which people travel, and which are counted as a tourist attraction, are a sign of Allah standing as proof of the destruction of their builders who denied the messengers. The Truth, glory be to Him, has left no excuse for any of His creatures, after He revealed to them the cosmic signs that testify to His oneness and divinity, and the miracles that establish the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from his Lord, then the verses of rulings that carry the governance of life, which no human can improve upon, and which contain the healing cure and the effective remedy for every disease of society. Then after that He left them to deny the deniers before their eyes, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning (137) and at night. Will you not reason?﴾ (138) [as-Saffat].

Behold, the remains of 'Ad, Thamud and others still bear witness against them: some above the earth, and most buried beneath layers of soil. Therefore we find that all ancient ruins are discovered in excavations beneath the ground. And why not, when a single gust of wind would sweep up an entire caravan, so consider the blasts of wind from the days of 'Ad until now. So: take a lesson from the fate of these people.

The meaning of ﴿Have they not been guided...﴾ (26) [as-Sajdah]: "yahdi" means: it indicates, guides, shows and clarifies. Guidance has three elements: a guide, one who is guided, and the thing to which one is guided. The root (h-d-y) is used in the Book of Allah in three ways:

The first: the Guide is mentioned, who is Allah, mighty and majestic. The second: the one guided is mentioned, who are the creatures. The third: the destination to which one is guided, which is the goal that Allah wants.

This verb sometimes takes its object directly, as in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿Guide us to the straight path (6)﴾ [al-Fatihah], meaning: O Allah, Allah is the Guide, we are the guided, and the goal is the straight path.

Sometimes the verb takes the preposition "li-" (to/for), as in: ﴿And they say, "Praise to Allah, who guided us to this."﴾ (43) [al-A'raf]. He did not say "guided us this." Sometimes it takes "ila" (to), as in: ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ (213) [al-Baqarah].

You notice that the Guide is one, namely Allah the Exalted, and the guided are the creatures; but the destination guided to is what varies. In this verse, however, the matter differs, for He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Have they not been guided [li-hum]...﴾ (26) [as-Sajdah]. The preposition "li-" has not been attached to the destination; rather it has been attached to the guided. He did not say: "Has Allah not guided these people to such-and-such."

So why?

They said: because some people think that when God guides you to the path He burdens you with the hardships of obligations; therefore we see some people recoiling.

Firstly, you should notice here the harmony of the Qur'anic arrangement between the beginning of the verses and their end. In the previous verse He, glorified is He, said ﴿Did it not guide them?﴾ [As-Sajdah 26], meaning: does it not show or guide. The discussion there concerns historical narratives, so it fits with ﴿Do they not hear?﴾ [As-Sajdah 26]. Here, however, the discussion concerns visible scenes, so it fits with ﴿Do they not see?﴾ [As-Sajdah 27]. This is because what is heard should be heard, and what is seen should be seen.

In the previous verse He said ﴿We destroyed...﴾ [As-Sajdah 26], so that we may take a lesson from the destruction of the deniers in the past. Here, however, He draws our attention to one of His signs in the cosmos, so the verb comes as ﴿We drive the water...﴾ [As-Sajdah 27] in the present tense, which indicates renewal and continuity. At all times God drives the clouds, and rain falls from them onto the earth (al-juruz), meaning the barren land, which then becomes green with all kinds of crops and fruits. This is a continuous sign that we all see, and it persists in the present and in the future. Because this sign is happening now, it requires from us observation and contemplation, so He said, in its service, ﴿Do they not see?﴾ [As-Sajdah 27].

In another place He said: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed. And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren, lifeless ground.﴾ [Al-Kahf 7-8]. Al-juruz is the land from which vegetation has been cut off, either because water has been withheld from it so it has dried up, or because it has matured and been harvested.

The meaning of ﴿We drive the water...﴾ [As-Sajdah 27]: al-sawq (driving) is urging with speed. Therefore you say to one who hurries you, "Why are you driving us like this?" It is known that driving is from behind, unlike leading (al-qiyadah), which is from the front. Whatever you drive, you drive while it is in front of you; you see it and it does not escape from you. If it is behind you, it is liable to flee from you, and you do not perceive it.

Driving is sometimes applied to clouds, as in the saying of God Most High: ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land...﴾ [Fatir 9].

Sometimes driving is applied to the water itself, as in this verse, and the driving of water has several aspects: God drives water from the clouds to the earth, and when it descends to the earth, He drives it in rivers, or makes it flow as springs in the earth to keep it for us until we need it.

Our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has made for us reservoirs of water beneath the earth, not so that we may hoard it when it is available, but so that we may find it when it is lost. The fact that water becomes springs in the earth enables us to overcome many problems: the earth preserves it for us, so it does not evaporate, and we do not need to build dams and other things, which preserves for us the sweet water.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain that fell upon land. Part of it was fertile ground that absorbed the water and produced grass and vegetation. Part of it was hard ground that held the water, so people drank from it, watered their livestock and crops. And part of it was barren plains that neither hold water nor produce vegetation. That is the likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me."¹

These are three types of land representing people's benefit from knowledge. The first holds water and yields crops; the second holds water so that people benefit from it. You may ask: what is the benefit of the third, the barren plains that hold no water and produce no vegetation? And why did God create them then?

We say: these barren plains are the ones through which water passes into the depths of the earth. God spoke the truth: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky and made you drink it, and you are not its keepers.﴾ [Al-Hijr 22]. And He said: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken, who could bring you flowing water?﴾ [Al-Mulk 30].

So these plains have a purpose known to whoever reflects on this matter; otherwise God, Exalted is He, never created anything in vain. Likewise, people benefit from knowledge: some of them we see the effect of their knowledge immediately, while for others the benefit of their knowledge is delayed for future generations.

Then beware of supposing that when God makes water flow as springs beneath the earth, it spreads through it in a random manner, or that sweet water mixes with salt water through a fluid passage. No. Rather, the sweet water flows in something like special pipes and channels, which they find even beneath the salt waters of the gulf.

These are among the wonders of creation that show the power of the Creator, Mighty and Majestic. Just as there is a barrier between the two seas on the earth's surface ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side. Between them is a barrier they do not transgress﴾ [Ar-Rahman 19-20], so there is also a barrier between the two waters beneath the earth.

God, Glorified is He, draws our attention to this visible sign ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land...﴾ [As-Sajdah 27]. Yes, this is a sign that we all see, but what is meant here is a seeing of deep reflection, remembrance, admonition and understanding, through which we are guided to the power of the Creator, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, glorified is He, ﴿We drive...﴾ [As-Sajdah 27], contains evidence of His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) over creation. Although the driving of water is carried out through the angels entrusted with it, He, Exalted is He, is the original authority and the one who follows the process of its execution.

God, Glorified is He, placed the livestock before humans in eating from the crops, even though all of them belong to humans, because livestock generally do not eat from the crops while they are still green and unripe, leaving them for humans to eat. Also, when He, glorified is He, feeds the livestock, He is feeding from what He made as fruit and food for humans, namely the livestock.

We have pointed out that the precision of Qur'anic expression required that this visible sign conclude with His saying, ﴿Do they not see?﴾ [As-Sajdah 27], because this matter relates to sight.

In such precision you may read His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?﴾ [Al-Qasas 71]. ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?﴾ [Al-Qasas 72].

In the first He said ﴿Then will you not hear?﴾ [Al-Qasas 71] because it speaks of the sign of the night, and hearing is the means of perception in it. In the other He said ﴿Then will you not see?﴾ [Al-Qasas 72] because it speaks of the sign of the day, and sight is the means of perception in the day. So observe the precision of expression and its inimitability, for the Speaker is God and Lord, so every word must be in its appropriate place.

¹ Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/399), and by his son Abdullah in his additions to the Musnad (4/399), and by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (79), Book of Knowledge (20), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (2282), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ (32:28).

("Mata," "when"), is used to ask about time, and asking with it indicates that you consider the matter slow in coming, so you ask: when will it occur?

When the Messenger (ﷺ) was sent, he informed his people that he was being sent to them with a method from God, that God had supported him with miracles, and he informed them of the fate of those who followed him and the fate of those who opposed him. He told them that his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, would not send him to them and then abandon him or leave him alone; he would certainly prevail over them. This is the way of God with His prophets and messengers, as He said, glorified is He: ﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ [As-Saffat].

Therefore we have said: if you see a situation in which the Muslims did not prevail, even during the lifetime of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the lifetime of the Companions, know that the conditions of soldiership among them had become defective, so they were not, in a state of defeat, devoted soldiers of God.

When we reflect on the events at (Uhud), we find that God the Exalted says to the Muslims: do not think that the presence of the Messenger of God among you will protect you or exempt you from this matter. This is a law of God in His creation that does not change.

At (Uhud), the Muslims disobeyed the orders of the Messenger of God, when the archers descended and left their positions out of desire for the spoils, so the polytheists encircled them, and the result was – we do not say they were defeated, rather they did not achieve victory – because the battle was (ma'at) (thrown into confusion) while the Messenger was present among them.(1)

Some see in this outcome of the battle of Uhud a point of criticism, saying: how can an army led by the Messenger of God be defeated? But this matter counts for the Messenger, not against him. The Messenger would not live among them forever, and they had to see with their own eyes the consequence of disobeying the Messenger of God's command, and to feel the sanctity of these orders. Had they won while disobeying, they would have lost confidence in the Messenger's orders afterward. And why not, since they had disobeyed him at Uhud and won!

Likewise on the day of Hunayn, about which God said: ﴿And [recall] the day of Hunayn, when your large number pleased you but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with its vastness...﴾ (9:25) [At-Tawbah].

Among the believers' admiration of their large numbers was that Abu Bakr himself said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." So God the Exalted taught them a lesson, and they nearly were defeated, had God not overtaken them in the end with His mercy, and the scale of the battle turned in their favor. It was as though the disciplining came in proportion to the disobedience.

So the Truth, glorified is He, teaches us to comply with His command, to be sincere in soldiership for God, glorified is He, and to be disciplined in it so that we reach its goal. If we disobey, we are deprived of this goal, because if I gave you the goal while you disobeyed, my command would have no place of respect or reverence.

Here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, relates the polytheists' saying to the Messenger of God: ﴿When is this victory...?﴾ (32:28) [As-Sajdah], meaning: the victory which God promised you. This victory was a distant goal for the believers, for they were still a small, oppressed group.

Therefore, when God's saying was revealed: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and they will turn their backs﴾ (54:45) [Al-Qamar], Umar was astonished and said: "What multitude will be routed? We cannot even protect ourselves!" But the Truth, glorified is He, did not prolong this situation for them. Badr came swiftly, and Umar saw with his own eyes how God's promise was fulfilled and how the host of the polytheists was defeated. After the battle he himself repeated it: "Yes, O Lord, the multitude will be put to flight and they will turn their backs."(2)

It is remarkable that the Messenger of God pointed out to the unbelievers and to his companions and helpers, by God's overflowing favor upon him, that he informed them of the outcome of the battle before it occurred. He stood on the land of Badr and pointed with a staff in his hand at the places where the polytheists would fall: "This is the place where Abu Jahl will fall, this is where Utbah will fall, and this is where al-Walid will fall."(3) etc.

Who can determine the outcome of a battle in such detail, when battle is back-and-forth, attack and retreat, and mixing, especially since they had not set out for war, but only to intercept the Quraysh trade caravan? So what of if they had set out in a state of readiness for war? The unbelievers would take this as a measure by which to gauge the strength of the nascent Muslims; God would cast fear of this outcome into the hearts of the unbelievers. And why not, since the small, oppressed, unequipped group triumphed over the arrogant multitude prepared for war.

The interrogative here, ﴿When is this victory...?﴾ (32:28) [As-Sajdah], is not a question in its literal sense; it is intended as mockery and derision. God's answer to this question defines their intention behind it. They consider this victory and this dominance, which God promised to His believing servants, to be far off, yet they hasten toward a matter that is coming and undoubted.

The Qur'an recorded this same attitude against them in His saying, the Exalted, relating the unbelievers saying to their messenger: ﴿So bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful.﴾ (7:70) [Al-A'raf].

The word (al-fath) (the victory/opening): if it comes with the definite article "al," then its good is affirmed; know that it is a protected blessing whose benefit will reach you. If it comes indefinite, it necessarily needs a complement that clarifies its purpose: is this victory for you or against you? God's saying in addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾ (48:1) [Al-Fath] indicates that this victory is for his benefit (ﷺ), so it is gain without loss, as they say in bank accounts: "in his favor and against him."

As for the other, it is in God's saying: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of every good thing...﴾ (6:44) [Al-An'am].

So then: be alert to what God opens for you, do not be deceived by it, and consider: is it for you or against you? Beware lest blessing make you rebellious when the world smiles upon you, for perhaps it is a gradual leading astray while you are unaware. The fath (opening) bears both meanings. Read, if you wish:

﴿And if the people of the cities had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth...﴾ (7:96) [Al-A'raf], meaning: beware this blessing lest it make you rebellious.

The word (al-fath) comes with multiple meanings, determined by context, as we said regarding the word (ayn). It comes meaning the seeing eye: you say, "I saw so-and-so with my eye." You say, "I gave generously to so-and-so with ('ayn) from me," meaning gold or silver. You say, "I allowed him to irrigate his land from my ('ayn)," meaning a spring of water. You say, "These are so-and-so's ('uyun)," meaning his spies. This is what they call the homonym (al-mushtarak al-lafzi).

The word (al-fath) is used first for the material matter. You say, "I opened (fataḥtu) the door," meaning I removed its bolts. This is the original meaning of fath. God the Exalted says in the story of Prophet Joseph, peace be upon him: ﴿And when they opened their goods, they found their merchandise returned to them...﴾ (12:65) [Yusuf], where "fataḥu matā'ahum" is the material opening that removes its bindings.

It may also refer to the immaterial opening, as in God's saying: ﴿And when some of them meet others, they say, "Do you talk to them about what God has opened to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord...?"﴾ (2:76) [Al-Baqarah], meaning: what God has given you and bestowed upon you of good and knowledge.

Fath also means the manifestation of truth in judging between right and wrong and clarifying the matter; for this reason the people of Yemen call the judge (al-fatih).

It means victory and dominance, as in this verse before us: ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ (32:28). The believers must answer this question: we do not say that we are truthful or untruthful regarding this report, because this is a matter distant from us and none of our concern; it is from God, who informed us of this report, so we are not described in it as truthful or false.

For a person to be just, he must attribute the act to its doer. Did you see that when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) informed his people of his Night Journey, he said: "Verily I was taken by night from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis"(4), and did not say "I traveled," yet the people still asked him: "Do you claim you went there in one night, when we spend a month driving camels' livers to it?" This was a sophistry from them, not a failure to understand the Messenger's statement, for they were a people of speech who understood well the meanings of words.

So then: the Messenger of God did not travel by his own essence; rather God made him travel. Whoever wishes to examine this matter should examine it in the light of God's power and how time is with respect to God, the Exalted. We have said: an act that takes time is a treated act, but our Lord, blessed and exalted, does not treat acts; He merely says "Be," and it is. The act's duration is inversely proportional to the strength of the agent: whenever the agent's power increases, the act's time decreases. Accordingly, if you attribute the event of the Night Journey to the power of the Truth, blessed and exalted, you will find that time is no time.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, answers their question, "When will this victory be?" (32:28), in a way that indicates that it was a question of disbelief and mockery, so He says, may He be glorified:

"Say: On the Day of Victory, their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved, nor will they be reprieved." (32:29)

That is: Why do you ask about the Day of Victory? And what benefit would knowledge of it be to you? When the Day of Victory comes, it lowers the curtain over your crimes. Neither repentance nor faith will benefit you on it, and God will not grant you respite until another time.

It is well known that faith benefits its possessor only if he has a margin of time. As for the faith that comes at the final death throes, when the soul has reached the throat, it is like the faith of Pharaoh, who said when drowning overtook him: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims" (10:90). God rejected this faith of his: "Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters?" (10:91).

Now faith will not benefit you, because you are turning toward God, the time for action has passed, and the first reckoning has come. Faith is to believe while you are eager, healthy, facing life and loving it; faith is to believe by choice.

"Nor will they be reprieved" (32:29): that is, there is no respite for you now, because the One who created you knows your inner secrets, and knows that if He gave you respite you would return to what you were upon: "And if they were returned, they would certainly revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars" (6:28).

Note 1: Qatadah said: "al-Fath" means the judgment. Al-Farra' and al-Qutaybi said: it means the conquest of Makkah. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5371): better than this is what Mujahid said, that he said: it means the Day of Resurrection.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are waiting.﴾ (32:30)

This meaning is like what we say in colloquial Arabic: "Idini 'arid katafak" (give me your shoulder to turn away), that is, depart from them. There is no longer any meeting between you and them, and no benefit in debating them or arguing with them, for they have exhausted every means of persuasion. Nothing remains for them except the sword to restrain them, in accordance with the words of the poet:

Patience, and if it does not suffice, then after it a threat;
and if resolve does not suffice, then resolve itself will suffice.

The Messenger of Allah conveyed to them and warned them. He gave them the good news of Paradise for whoever believes, and warned them of the Fire for whoever disbelieves, but they did not listen. Therefore:

There is nothing but revelation, or a sharp blade;
the intelligent is persuaded by revelation, and the ignorant is restrained by the sword.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And wait...﴾ (32:30), it is a command from Allah Most High to His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, meaning: wait for My promise to you of victory and triumph. We have said that the promise of Allah is certain, since there is no other power that can prevent Him from fulfilling His promise. As for the human being, when he promises, he must be mindful of his humanness and that he possesses none of the means to carry out what he has promised.

Therefore our Lord teaches us: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23) except [when adding], "If Allah wills"...(24)﴾ (18:23–24). Making your matter contingent upon the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, protects you from being a liar if you do not fulfill what you promised, for the means of fulfilling a promise are not possessed by humans; they are possessed by the Creator of humans, glorified is He. So when He promises, know that His promise is certain to come to pass.

We have said that when you tell your companion, for example: "I will meet you tomorrow" or "I will do such-and-such for you," you are truthful and intend to fulfill it, but you do not possess tomorrow a single one of the means of fulfilling it; something may arise unexpectedly, or an obstacle may prevent you, or perhaps your opinion may change... etc.

There is a difference between the waiting of the Messenger of Allah, when he executes the command of his Lord, ﴿And wait...﴾ (32:30), and ﴿indeed, they are waiting﴾ (32:30). The waiting of the Messenger of Allah is for something certain, backed by strength and power, whereas their waiting is a self's whispering and a devil's suggestion, having no backing of enforcing power.

The meaning of ﴿indeed, they are waiting﴾ (32:30) is: they wait for something to happen to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that would prevent him from conveying the message of his Lord. This is foolishness on their part, for they should have known that the Messenger is supported by Allah and sent from Him to guide them, and Allah would not send a messenger and then abandon or forsake him. The sunnah of Allah regarding the messengers is that they are victorious, however strong the strength of those who oppose them may become.

Therefore: there is no way to that, nor any way to escape from it, or even to frighten him so that he desists and abandons what he calls to from the methodology of his Lord.

This waiting occurs in another place with the word (al-tarabbus) in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Wait, indeed I am with you among those who wait.﴾ (52:31)

And in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best things?..."﴾ (9:52), meaning: what do you await for us, while we await for you one of two good outcomes: either victory and triumph over you, whereupon we would drive you away and humiliate you; or martyrdom, which guarantees us an everlasting life of bliss. ﴿And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him or by our hands, so wait...﴾ (9:52).

That is: wait for us, and we too wait for you, but there is a difference between our waiting and your waiting.

This surah was named "al-Sajda" (The Prostration) first because in it is a prostration of recitation, at which we should prostrate to Allah in gratitude. Prostration represents the utmost submission to the Truth, blessed and exalted is He. So when this verse comes, which shakes the being of a person, our Lord teaches us to respond to the shaking of the being and to hasten to prostrate, and not to wait for our prostration until later in prayer.

So in this verse there is a powerful command and a great secret that called for taking prostration out of its place by the command of the one who legislated the first prostration. Therefore there must be beautiful energies in the verses of prostration of recitation, graces of Allah that remind me of Him.

Allah, glorified is He, wants creation to feel that they are receiving new blessings, for which the familiar regular prostration is not sufficient thanks; so He legislates for them a prostration specific to them.

Also in the surah are some allusions which those who have knowledge have stood upon, and they said: they set out models for preserving the human soul and not distancing it from the wisdom of its Creator. Among these allusions: the eye sees things and says, "This is beautiful, and this is ugly"; that is merely from the outward form, but a person should contemplate things and know the meaning of ugliness.

Ugliness is not what seems ugly in your view; rather, the ugly is that which removes the legal good from its proper standard, because the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, created everything beautiful, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿who perfected everything He created...﴾ (32:7).

So if a thing seems ugly in your view, know that you have looked at the aspect of form and neglected other aspects, and say: "I have not yet attained the secret of its beauty."

We have previously said that the Creator, glorified is He, has scattered gifts among His creation, such that the total of each person's gifts equals the total of every other person's gifts. So do not look at one aspect and say, "This one is rich, and this one is poor," but look at the other aspects.

It is related that our master Noah, peace be upon him, saw a mangy dog and spat on it, whereupon Allah made the mangy dog speak and said to him: "Do you blame me or do you blame my Creator?" The meaning is that He created me for a wisdom and for some meaning.

And the one who said it spoke truly:

Ugliness has a time in which its beauty appears,
and the one who plastered the building is praised at the time of its demolition.

Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, has scattered His wisdom, and has scattered His goodness in His Book, so one verse does not replace another verse, nor one word another word, nor one letter another letter; but it is the insights that receive from Allah that are able to stand upon the secrets of Allah.
